articles.title: Iran's attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz escalate
articles.dek: Iran takes the offensive with attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and airstrikes on several countries around the Persian Gulf.

paragraphs.en: Iran takes the offensive with attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and airstrikes on several countries around the Persian Gulf.
paragraphs.zh: 伊朗发起进攻，对霍尔木兹海峡的船只进行攻击，并对波斯湾周边的几个国家进行空袭。

paragraphs.en: Iran's attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz are ramping up. Data shows attacks have hit a record high since the start of the war. And it's not just ships that are blowing up in the Gulf. The U.S. has been striking an Iranian island. And Iran has launched drones at U.S. radars and air defense systems in two Arab Gulf countries. Joining us to talk about all these escalations is NPR correspondent in Dubai, Aya Batrawy. So let's start with the Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. What makes this period different from others during the war?
paragraphs.zh: 伊朗对霍尔木兹海峡船只的袭击正在升级。数据显示，自战争开始以来，袭击次数已达到创纪录的高点。而在海湾中爆炸的并不仅仅是船只。美国一直在打击伊朗的一个岛屿。伊朗也向两个阿拉伯海湾国家的美国雷达和防空系统发射了无人机。加入我们讨论所有这些升级事件的是NPR驻迪拜记者Aya Batrawy。那么，让我们先从伊朗对霍尔木兹海峡船只的袭击开始。这一时期与战争期间的其他时期有何不同？

paragraphs.en: AYA BATRAWY, BYLINE: So, A, it's simply the sheer number of attacks. So in just one 24-hour period this week, Iran struck two ships, an oil tanker and another one carrying liquefied gas. And that vessel that was carrying gas exploded into a ball of fire. And the Indian crewmembers had to jump straight into the water without time to even get on lifeboats.
paragraphs.zh: 阿雅·巴特拉维，署名：所以，A，这只是攻击次数的数量。就在本周的一个24小时内，伊朗袭击了两艘船，一艘油轮和另一艘运送液化气的船。那艘运送天然气的船爆炸成一团火球。印度船员不得不直接跳入水中，甚至没有时间乘坐救生艇。

paragraphs.en: BATRAWY: That's according to Indian officials. Yeah. And Oman says its forces rescued the 24 men. But then also a tanker belonging to Abu Dhabi's oil company was struck that same day, with 11 crewmembers on that hospitalized and one missing. So this is a glimpse of just one day this week. They've been hitting ships daily. Now, the International Maritime Organization has some figures based on confirmed incidents, which I'll note here are conservative because not all crews report attacks.
paragraphs.zh: BATRAWY：这是根据印度官员的说法。是的。而阿曼表示，其部队救出了24人。但同一天，属于阿布扎比石油公司的油轮也遭遇袭击，船上11名船员住院，1人失踪。这只是本周一天的情况。他们每天都在攻击船只。现在，国际海事组织根据已确认的事件提供了一些数据，我在这里指出，这些数据是保守的，因为并非所有船员都会报告袭击事件。

paragraphs.en: But even with that in mind, there were far more attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz in October than any month since the start of the war. And November is on pace to exceed that. And, obviously, this isn't just keeping oil prices high. It's also killing seafarers. Bulk carriers with fertilizers and other essential products from the Gulf are also facing similar threats. And some of these tankers have sunk or spilled their oil out.
paragraphs.zh: 但即便考虑到这一点，10月份在霍尔木兹海峡对船只的袭击仍比战争开始以来的任何一个月份都多。而11月的情况可能会超过这个数字。显然，这不仅仅是让油价保持高位。这同样在危害海员的生命。从海湾运送化肥和其他必需品的散货船也面临类似的威胁。其中一些油轮已经沉没或泄漏了石油。

paragraphs.en: BATRAWY: All right. So for several weeks, there were huge stretches of the UAE's coastline that were closed to the public after an oil tanker was struck on October 9. And that oil slick washed up on the shores of various emirates here. And the cleanup effort is ongoing in some of these places. So I want to share with you what I saw this week when I drove up to the emirate of Umm Al Quwain, where its entire coast is still closed off to the public.
paragraphs.zh: BATRAWY：好吧。几周以来，在10月9日一艘油轮被撞后，阿联酋海岸线的大片区域对公众关闭。那次泄漏的油污冲到了这里各酋长国的海岸上。在一些地方，清理工作仍在进行中。所以我想和你们分享我这周开车前往乌姆盖万酋长国时看到的景象，那里的整个海岸线仍然对公众封闭。

paragraphs.en: I'm approaching an area with some benches that overlook the water. And the whole area smells like petrol. This is another consequence of this war that is now in its ninth month. I think this is the cleanup crew. I can see them cleaning up here. They're all wearing the hazard outfits.
paragraphs.zh: 我正接近一个有几张长椅的区域，这些长椅可以俯瞰水面。整个区域都弥漫着汽油味。这是这场已经持续到第九个月战争的另一个后果。我想这是清理队。我看到他们正在这里清理。他们都穿着防护服。

paragraphs.en: BATRAWY: Yeah. So it smelled like petrol. And, look, these Gulf Arab countries, they don't want to have to seek permission and pay transit fees to Iran to use a waterway that was free to navigate before this war. So the U.S. is escorting ships that want to pass the strait. But attacks continue.
paragraphs.zh: BATRAWY：是的。所以它闻起来像汽油。而且，你看，这些海湾阿拉伯国家，他们不想为了使用在这场战争之前可以自由通行的水道而不得不向伊朗寻求许可并支付过境费。所以美国正在护送想通过海峡的船只。但袭击仍在继续。

articles.title: AI giant Anthropic's shares pop in debut after blockbuster IPO
articles.dek: Shares in the AI juggernaut Anthropic are now trading on the stock market. They debuted Thursday, after a record-breaking IPO.

paragraphs.en: Shares in the AI juggernaut Anthropic are now trading on the stock market. They debuted Thursday, after a record-breaking IPO.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能巨头Anthropic的股票现在在股市交易。它们在创纪录的首次公开募股后于周四首次亮相。

paragraphs.en: Shares in the AI juggernaut Anthropic are now trading on the stock market. They debuted today after a record-breaking IPO.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能巨头Anthropic的股票现在在股市交易。它们在创纪录的首次公开募股后今天首次亮相。

paragraphs.en: ADENA FRIEDMAN: Today, Anthropic becomes a public company and begins trading on NASDAQ under the ticker symbol ANT.
paragraphs.zh: 阿德娜·弗里德曼：今天，Anthropic 成为一家上市公司，并开始在纳斯达克交易，股票代码为 ANT。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: The chair and CEO of NASDAQ celebrated the listing this morning. The CEO of Anthropic, Dario Amodei, had a big grin when he rang the opening bell.
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：纳斯达克的董事长兼首席执行官今天早上庆祝了上市。Anthropic 的首席执行官 Dario Amodei 在敲响开盘钟时露出了灿烂的笑容。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: And speaking of Anthropic and speaking of money, here is where we do have to note that Anthropic is a financial supporter of NPR. NPR's John Ruwitch is on the line from Silicon Valley with more from today. Hey, John.
paragraphs.zh: DETROW: 说到Anthropic，也说到钱，我们确实需要注意的是，Anthropic是NPR的财务支持者。NPR的约翰·鲁维奇现在从硅谷连线，为我们带来今天的最新情况。嗨，约翰。

paragraphs.en: RUWITCH: It was big. Anthropic sold nearly a billion shares to the public and sold others at the same time to a handful of big tech firms in what's known as a private placement. The total haul for the company, its founders, was more than $107 billion, with a B. The IPO alone was the biggest in history, blowing past SpaceX's listing from June, which had set the previous record.
paragraphs.zh: RUWITCH：规模很大。Anthropic 向公众出售了近十亿股股票，同时以所谓的私募方式向少数大型科技公司出售了其他股票。公司及其创始人的总收入超过了 1070 亿美元，仅首次公开募股（IPO）就创下了历史最大纪录，远超今年六月 SpaceX 的上市，后者此前创造了纪录。

paragraphs.en: You know, IPOs are kind of a two-step process. The company sells the shares at a fixed price to investors who apply in advance to get in on the IPO. That price was 83 bucks, which was higher than expected. And then the shares start trading on the stock market, which is what happened today, and they started out with a bang, opening up 34% from the IPO price. Now, they've come down off of the high over the course of the trading day, but they did end trading still well above the IPO price.
paragraphs.zh: 你知道，首次公开募股（IPO）有点像一个两步走的过程。公司以固定价格向提前申请参与IPO的投资者出售股票。那个价格是83美元，比预期的要高。然后股票开始在证券市场交易，这就是今天发生的情况，并且它们开盘表现非常好，开盘价比IPO价格上涨了34%。现在，在交易日内股价已经从高点回落，但收盘时仍然远高于IPO价格。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: What's interesting here is there's so many worries about AI right now, and one of the big worries is that, you know, the industry is possibly in a big bubble. Given that, why do you think investors were so eager to snap up these shares?
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：这里有趣的是，现在人们对人工智能有这么多担忧，其中一个大担忧是，你知道，这个行业可能正处于一个大泡沫中。既然如此，你认为为什么投资者如此急于抢购这些股票？

articles.title: OpenAI announces new AI safety program; researchers worry it won't be enough
articles.dek: AI safety researchers say OpenAI's new third party evaluator program falls far short of what the company promised, raising concerns about its effectiveness.

paragraphs.en: AI safety researchers say OpenAI's new third party evaluator program falls far short of what the company promised, raising concerns about its effectiveness.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能安全研究人员表示，OpenAI 新推出的第三方评估者计划远未达到公司承诺的水平，这引发了人们对其有效性的担忧。

paragraphs.en: The company announced Monday that staff from four AI safety and research organizations will become "embedded assessors" to "give people a clearer view of how labs are evaluating and managing [potential] risks."
paragraphs.zh: 公司周一宣布，来自四个人工智能安全和研究组织的员工将成为“嵌入式评估员”，以“让人们更清楚地了解实验室如何评估和管理[潜在]风险。”

paragraphs.en: "Getting an outside opinion on the safety work and the robustness of these systems is going to be increasingly important and valuable," CEO Sam Altman said at Semafor's Silicon Valley and the World conference on Monday.
paragraphs.zh: 首席执行官萨姆·奥特曼（Sam Altman）在周一的Semafor硅谷与世界大会上表示：“对这些系统的安全工作和稳健性获得外部意见将变得越来越重要和有价值。”

paragraphs.en: However, many AI safety researchers say the new program is a far cry from Altman's vow in September that independent evaluators would have "employee-like access" to internal company systems.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，许多人工智能安全研究人员表示，这个新项目与奥特曼在九月份承诺的独立评估人员将拥有“类似员工的访问权限”使用公司内部系统的愿景相去甚远。

paragraphs.en: Altman's promise came after details of the Hugging Face attack by OpenAI's autonomous systems shook the AI field. Worries of the technology's catastrophic risk captured public attention, and rival Anthropic said it would set up such a program.
paragraphs.zh: 在OpenAI的自主系统袭击Hugging Face的细节震动了人工智能领域之后，Altman的承诺随之而来。人们对该技术可能带来的灾难性风险的担忧引起了公众的关注，而竞争对手Anthropic表示将建立这样的项目。

paragraphs.en: "We are giving deep access to some of the most sensitive tools and models our researchers use...that are the most important for assessing key, relevant and timely safety claims," said Lama Ahmad, OpenAI's frontier assurances lead, on X.
paragraphs.zh: OpenAI的前沿保障负责人Lama Ahmad在X上表示：“我们正在向我们的研究人员使用的一些最敏感的工具和模型提供深度访问权限……这些工具和模型对于评估关键、相关和及时的安全声明至关重要。”

paragraphs.en: Prior to these new embedded evaluation programs, AI companies have brought in outside researchers to assess the capabilities of AI models and identify safety loopholes the companies have missed.
paragraphs.zh: 在这些新的嵌入式评估程序出现之前，人工智能公司曾邀请外部研究人员来评估人工智能模型的能力，并识别公司忽略的安全漏洞。

paragraphs.en: The work of outside evaluators have already helped shed light on the companies' work, and have raised public awareness of safety risks that the technology poses. One recent report about Anthropic using AI to significantly speed up model development has prompted concerns in the field about how close the top companies are to using AI to autonomously build even more powerful models, a stage known as recursive self-improvement. Some in the field worry that if this happens, the velocity of development could lead to catastrophic consequences for humanity and are calling for new regulation against the practice.
paragraphs.zh: 外部评估人员的工作已经帮助揭示了公司的工作，并提高了公众对该技术带来的安全风险的认识。最近一份关于Anthropic使用人工智能显著加快模型开发的报告，引发了该领域对顶尖公司距离使用人工智能自主构建更强大模型的阶段（称为递归自我改进）有多近的担忧。该领域的一些人担心，如果发生这种情况，开发速度可能导致对人类的灾难性后果，因此呼吁对这一做法进行新的监管。

articles.title: They tried to torture him into leaving Iraq. He refused to abandon the nature he protects
articles.dek: Drought threatens Iraq’s marshes, risking one of the oldest ways of life

paragraphs.en: Drought threatens Iraq’s marshes, risking one of the oldest ways of life
paragraphs.zh: 干旱威胁伊拉克的沼泽地，危及最古老的生活方式之一

paragraphs.en: CENTRAL MARSHES, southern Iraq — For all he's been through, environmentalist Jassim al-Asadi still approaches each sighting of wildlife in Iraq's marshes as if it's the very first time — even though he has seen them thousands of times before.
paragraphs.zh: 伊拉克南部中央沼泽——尽管经历过这么多，环保主义者贾西姆·阿尔-阿萨迪在看到伊拉克沼泽的野生动物时，仍然像第一次见到一样——即便他以前已经见过成千上万次。

paragraphs.en: "Do you see?" he asks excitedly, pointing out a white egret perched on the back of a water buffalo as his long, narrow boat glides by. "It's a buffalo! With a bird on its back!"
paragraphs.zh: “你看到了吗？”他兴奋地问，指着一只停在水牛背上的白鹭，当他那条又长又窄的小船滑过时。“是一头水牛！背上还有一只鸟！”

paragraphs.en: Kingfishers with bright flashes of blue on their wings perch on reeds rising up from the shallow water. A wild boar and her piglets dart in front of the boat and disappear into the tangled grass.
paragraphs.zh: 翠鸟翅膀上闪烁着明亮的蓝色，栖息在从浅水中长出的芦苇上。一只野猪和她的小猪在船前疾驰，然后消失在杂乱的草丛中。

paragraphs.en: Despite having been kidnapped, tortured and accused by an Iran-backed militia of being an Israeli agent, Asadi is back in the marshes, monitoring water levels and talking to fishermen and buffalo herders to find out what difference a season of rain has made in the biggest wetlands in the Middle East.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管曾被绑架、折磨并被一个伊朗支持的民兵指控为以色列特工，阿萨迪现在回到了湿地，监测水位，与渔民和水牛牧民交谈，以了解一季降雨在中东最大的湿地中带来了什么变化。

paragraphs.en: Five devastating years of drought dried out some of the marshlands. In places where water remained, it was brackish, stunting the reeds and grass. Water buffalo were dying from lack of food and contaminated water.
paragraphs.zh: 五年毁灭性的干旱让一些沼泽地干涸。在仍有水的地方，水是咸的，抑制了芦苇和草的生长。水牛因缺乏食物和被污染的水而死亡。

paragraphs.en: Residents who make their living from breeding the animals and selling milk and cream headed with their remaining herds in search of water or to the outskirts of southern Iraqi cities.
paragraphs.zh: 靠饲养动物和出售牛奶及奶油为生的居民带着剩余的牲畜，前往寻找水源或伊拉克南部城市的边缘地区。

paragraphs.en: They have now begun to return, repopulating some of the tiny floating islands where, aside from some modern technology, marsh residents live a way of life little changed since Sumerian times, more than 4,000 years ago.
paragraphs.zh: 他们现在已经开始返回，重新在一些微小的浮岛上定居，除了少量现代技术之外，这些沼泽居民的生活方式自4000多年前的苏美尔时期以来几乎没有改变。

paragraphs.en: Sylvester Stallone's underdog story Rocky was crowned the Best Picture at the 1977 Academy Awards. The film's most famous sequence shows the character Rocky Balboa training for his big heavyweight boxing championship.
paragraphs.zh: 西尔维斯特·史泰龙的逆袭故事《洛奇》在1977年奥斯卡颁奖礼上被评为最佳影片。电影中最著名的片段展示了角色洛奇·巴尔博亚为他的重量级拳击冠军赛进行训练。

paragraphs.en: He runs through trainyards, a crowded outdoor market, and a jogging path. He punches a speedbag, does push-ups and sit-ups, gets repeatedly jabbed in the stomach, and slugs frozen sides of beef with his bare knuckles. Finally, Rocky sprints up the steps of the Philadelphia Art Museum, all the way to the top, where he jumps up and down and raises his arms in triumph.
paragraphs.zh: 他穿过火车场、拥挤的露天市场和慢跑道。他打着速度包，做俯卧撑和仰卧起坐，肚子被反复戳，还用赤手空拳猛击冻牛肉。最后，洛基冲上费城艺术博物馆的台阶，一路冲到顶端，跳上跳下，举起双臂示意胜利。

paragraphs.en: Now the new movie I Play Rocky tells the story about how Stallone wrote and starred in his movie. It also celebrates the original cinematographer, Garrett Brown. He invented the Steadicam — which is still in use today.
paragraphs.zh: 现在我演的这部新电影《洛基》讲述了史泰龙如何编剧并主演他的电影的故事。它还庆祝了原摄像师加勒特·布朗。他发明了史蒂迪摄像机——直到今天仍在使用。

paragraphs.en: For Rocky, Brown used his invention to shoot from inside the boxing ring; he also wove through the frozen meat locker and ran up those steps with Rocky.
paragraphs.zh: 对于洛基，布朗用他的发明从拳击台内开枪；他还穿过冷冻肉库，并和洛基一起跑上那些台阶。

paragraphs.en: "He's not just holding a camera, he's telling a story," says I Play Rocky director Peter Farrelly. Garrett's smooth camera movements captured Rocky's iconic moment at the top of the stairs that still — a half-century later — has fans cheering wildly.
paragraphs.zh: 《我玩过洛基》的导演彼得·法雷利说：“他不仅仅是在拿着相机，他在讲述一个故事。”加勒特流畅的摄影动作捕捉到了洛基在楼梯顶端的标志性瞬间，这一时刻即便在半个世纪后，依然让观众热烈欢呼。

paragraphs.en: "Garrett Brown was smart enough and savvy enough and artistic enough," says Farrelly, "[that] he didn't just shoot him going up the stairs, he followed him around and we got to be part of it as an audience."
paragraphs.zh: Farrelly说：“Garrett Brown 足够聪明、足够精明、足够有艺术感，他不仅仅拍摄他上楼的画面，他还跟着他走动，而我们作为观众也得以参与其中。”

paragraphs.en: All the while, Brown was filming with his invention strapped to his chest.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，布朗胸前绑着他的发明进行拍摄。

paragraphs.en: "It has a harness instead of being in your hands," Brown tells NPR about his Steadicam. "And at the business end of that arm is a so-called gimbal, so that any angular thing that I did not get through to the camera."
paragraphs.zh: 布朗在接受NPR采访时谈到他的Steadicam：“它是一个挂带，而不是用手拿着。那根臂的末端是一个所谓的万向节，所以任何我没有传递给摄像机的角度动作都会通过它实现。”

paragraphs.en: Brown's contraption included a fiber optic viewfinder strapped to his head. "I can only imagine what that looked like," he chuckles. "You have to be immune to embarrassment to try out inventions like that."
paragraphs.zh: 布朗的装置包括一个绑在他头上的光纤取景器。“我只能想象那看起来是什么样子，”他笑着说。“要尝试那样的发明，你必须对尴尬免疫。”

articles.title: Karl Kani dressed hip-hop royalty for decades. Now he's telling his own story
articles.dek: Hip-hop streetwear pioneer Karl Kani shares how he built his brand in new memoir

paragraphs.en: Hip-hop streetwear pioneer Karl Kani shares how he built his brand in new memoir
paragraphs.zh: 嘻哈街头服饰先驱卡尔·卡尼在新回忆录中分享了他如何打造自己的品牌

paragraphs.en: Fashion designer Karl Kani believes hip-hop needed its own clothing brand, one that reflected the music, culture and style of the artists who were changing fashion in the 1990s.
paragraphs.zh: 时尚设计师卡尔·卡尼认为嘻哈需要自己的服装品牌，一个能够反映那些在1990年代改变时尚的艺术家的音乐、文化和风格的品牌。

paragraphs.en: "Hip-hop needed the clothing brand that fit that look, who was from the culture," Kani told NPR's A Martínez on Morning Edition. "And I felt like the marriage between Kani and hip-hop was, like, heaven-sent."
paragraphs.zh: 卡尼在《晨间版》节目中告诉 NPR 的 A·马丁内斯：“嘻哈需要符合那种外观的服装品牌，来自那个文化的品牌。我觉得卡尼和嘻哈之间的结合简直是天赐的。”

paragraphs.en: Kani, born Carl Williams, started designing clothing in Brooklyn, New York, in the late 1980s. He was inspired by watching his father, a Haitian tailor, make matching linen suits to sell around the neighborhood.
paragraphs.zh: 卡尼，本名卡尔·威廉姆斯，生于纽约布鲁克林，于20世纪80年代末开始设计服装。他的灵感来自于观察他的父亲——一位海地裁缝——制作成套亚麻西装在邻里间销售。

paragraphs.en: At the time, hip-hop artists were already wearing names like Ralph Lauren, Tommy Hilfiger and Calvin Klein. But they weren't necessarily wearing the clothes as their designers intended. They favored oversized fits, mixed colors and created looks of their own.
paragraphs.zh: 当时，嘻哈艺术家已经穿着拉尔夫·劳伦、汤米·希尔费格和卡尔文·克莱因等品牌的服装。但他们穿衣并不一定按照设计师的原意。他们喜欢超大尺码、混搭颜色，并创造自己独特的造型。

paragraphs.en: Kani understood the appeal. He began making clothes as a self-taught designer in Brooklyn, New York, in the late 1980s. He helped turn that emerging streetwear style into a brand worn by some of hip-hop's biggest stars, including Tupac Shakur, Aaliyah and The Notorious B.I.G.
paragraphs.zh: Kani理解这种吸引力。他在1980年代末在纽约布鲁克林自学成才，开始制作衣服。他帮助将那种新兴的街头服饰风格发展成一个被一些嘻哈界最大明星穿着的品牌，包括图派克·沙库尔、艾莉亚和著名的B.I.G.

paragraphs.en: But the designer's ambitions extended beyond dressing famous musicians. He wanted to build an international fashion business that could last.
paragraphs.zh: 但这位设计师的野心不仅仅是为著名音乐人设计服装。他想要建立一个能够持久发展的国际时尚企业。

paragraphs.en: In his new memoir, Karl Kani: A Life By Design, Kani reflects on the creative instincts and business decisions that helped his brand survive long after the decade that made it famous.
paragraphs.zh: 在他的新回忆录《凯尔·卡尼：设计人生》中，卡尼回顾了那些帮助他的品牌在成名的那个年代之后仍能存续的创意本能和商业决策。

articles.title: Nvidia hold first earnings call since former CEO's departure
articles.dek: Chip giant Nvidia held its first earnings call since the departure of former CEO Jensen Huang, as interim CEO Colette Kress takes over.

paragraphs.en: Chip giant Nvidia held its first earnings call since the departure of former CEO Jensen Huang, as interim CEO Colette Kress takes over.
paragraphs.zh: 芯片巨头英伟达在前首席执行官黄仁勋离职后进行了首次财报电话会议，由临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯接任。

paragraphs.en: Nvidia executives yesterday held their first earnings call since CEO Jensen Huang stepped down over allegations about extramarital affairs and possible spying attempts by China.
paragraphs.zh: 昨天，英伟达高管举行了自首席执行官黄仁勋因婚外情指控及中国可能的间谍行为尝试而辞职以来的首次财报电话会议。

paragraphs.en: And board chairman Harvey Jones shot down speculation that Huang might be brought back after vocal supporters mounted a Stand with Jensen campaign.
paragraphs.zh: 董事会主席哈维·琼斯驳斥了关于黄可能在公开支持者发起“支持詹森”活动后被召回的猜测。

paragraphs.en: HARVEY JONES: The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.
paragraphs.zh: 哈维·琼斯：英伟达董事会一致接受了他的辞职，并且无意重新任命詹森为首席执行官。

paragraphs.en: MARTÍNEZ: NPR tech correspondent John Ruwitch has been following the saga. John, it sounds like they are pretty clear about not wanting to bring Jensen Huang back. But beyond that, what were the main messages executives tried to get across?
paragraphs.zh: MARTÍNEZ：NPR科技记者约翰·鲁维奇一直在跟踪这一事件。约翰，看起来他们很明确地表示不想让黄仁勋回来。但除此之外，管理层试图传达的主要信息是什么？

paragraphs.en: JOHN RUWITCH, BYLINE: Yeah. Board chairman Harvey Jones clearly wanted to quash rumors right at the outset. It was notable that he said the board had unanimously agreed to accept Huang's resignation. And he also threw his support behind interim CEO Colette Kress, who has served as chief financial officer for years, and in Jones' words, has been at the center of the company's extraordinary growth. Now, Kress was also on the call, and she tried to project business as usual.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰·鲁维奇，署名：是的。董事会主席哈维·琼斯显然希望一开始就平息谣言。值得注意的是，他说董事会一致同意接受黄的辞职。他还表达了对临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯的支持，克雷斯多年来一直担任首席财务官，用琼斯的话说，她一直处于公司非凡增长的核心位置。现在，克雷斯也参加了电话会议，她试图展示一切如常。

paragraphs.en: COLETTE KRESS: Our ambition will not change. Our passion to innovate will not change. And our commitment to customers, partners and shareholders will not change.
paragraphs.zh: 科莱特·克雷斯：我们的雄心不会改变。我们对创新的热情不会改变。我们对客户、合作伙伴和股东的承诺也不会改变。

paragraphs.en: RUWITCH: She said, effectively, the company's doing great. Its customers and employees are sticking with it. And, A, get this - at the end, she ended the call by saying, we've got this.
paragraphs.zh: RUWITCH：她实际上说，公司做得很棒。它的客户和员工都在支持它。而且，听这个——最后，她在结束通话时说，我们可以应对这个。

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI is a grounded love story, a gonzo crime thriller and a gaming triumph
articles.dek: I want to tell you about the time I saw Bigfoot. I want to tell you about sitting in the rain on a city street in a muscle car and prepping to rob a bank while lightning split the sky between…

paragraphs.en: I want to tell you about the time I saw Bigfoot. I want to tell you about sitting in the rain on a city street in a muscle car and prepping to rob a bank while lightning split the sky between high-rise condo towers in the distance and the drum fill from In The Air Tonight played on the radio. I want to tell you about gunfights and fistfights, the perfect satire of radio commercials and how the sunrise looks over Ocean Beach. But more than any of that, I want to tell you about the time an alligator bit my mom.
paragraphs.zh: 我想告诉你我看到大脚怪的那段经历。我想告诉你我坐在城市街道的肌肉车里淋着雨的情景，以及在远处高层公寓塔楼间闪电劈开天空时，准备抢银行的经历，而《今夜空气中》的鼓声在收音机里响起。我想告诉你关于枪战和拳击，关于电台广告的完美讽刺，以及日出时海洋海滩的景色。但比起这些，我更想告诉你有一次一只鳄鱼咬了我妈妈的事情。

paragraphs.en: It happened in the backyard of an abandoned house with a rotting inground pool. My mom, Mia Caminos (mother of Lucia Caminos, one of the two leads in Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI, probably the most highly anticipated video game sequel of all time), was thrilled by the pool. Standing there, amid the artfully rendered weeds and trash, she spread her arms and told me to use my imagination, to see her vision for this ruin of a house with its upmarket water feature, in a scabby neighborhood on the outskirts of Vice City. She speaks in tones of increasingly frantic desperation because she has already put money down on this house, sight unseen. All of her money, actually, in hopes of flipping it and selling it fast to keep her startup real estate business afloat.
paragraphs.zh: 这件事发生在一座废弃房子的后院，那里有一个正在腐烂的地面游泳池。我的妈妈，Mia Caminos（Lucia Caminos的母亲，Lucia是《侠盗猎车手 VI》中两位主角之一，这可能是有史以来最令人期待的视频游戏续作），对这个游泳池感到非常兴奋。站在那里，在精心描绘的杂草和垃圾中，她张开双臂，告诉我用想象力去看她对这座废墟般的房子及其高档水景的设想，这座房子位于Vice City郊区的一个破旧社区。她的语气越来越带有惊慌和绝望，因为她已经在这所房子上下了钱，实际上是把她所有的钱都投入进去，希望能迅速翻修后出售，以维持她的创业房地产生意。

paragraphs.en: The pool is still half full of water. There's a dirty, sodden mattress floating in it. And as if this is the main thing standing between her and success, Mia is fixated on getting it out of the pool.
paragraphs.zh: 游泳池里仍然有一半是水。里面漂着一张又脏又湿的床垫。仿佛这就是她成功与否的主要障碍，米娅专注于把它从泳池里拿出来。

paragraphs.en: And, dutifully, I do. Playing as Lucia, I grab hold, mash buttons, help my mom drag away the wet, heavy, stinking mattress. And just as we get it up and over the lip of the pool that's going to be the thing that makes this wreck of a house suddenly desirable – that's when the alligator lunges out of the murky water, grabs my mom by the arm and tries to drag her back in.
paragraphs.zh: 于是，我尽职尽责地去做了。扮演卢西亚时，我抓住，把玩按钮，帮妈妈拖走那张湿漉漉、沉重、发臭的床垫。正当我们把它抬过游泳池的边缘——那个游泳池将使这座破旧的房子突然变得令人向往——就在这时，一只鳄鱼从浑浊的水中跃出，抓住我妈妈的手臂，试图把她拉回水里。

paragraphs.en: This is a story about folly, fixation, unrealistic expectations of success at the ass-end of late capitalism, and the vicious, whip-crack cruelty of predators who lie in wait for anyone trying to improve a terrible situation.
paragraphs.zh: 这是一个关于愚蠢、执着、对在晚期资本主义末端取得成功的不切实际的期望，以及潜伏的捕食者残酷、鞭打般的残忍——他们等待任何试图改善糟糕状况的人——的故事。

paragraphs.en: But then I shoot the alligator in the head before it can eat my mom. Because this is also a story about violence, and how sometimes (maybe all the times), the loud, cathartic rip of gunfire is the only solution left for people who have already lost so much and can't bear to see one more thing taken from them.
paragraphs.zh: 但后来我就朝鳄鱼的头部开枪，免得它吃掉我妈。因为这也是一个关于暴力的故事，有时（也许是所有时候），响亮的枪声是那些已经失去太多、再也无法忍受看到自己被夺走一切的人唯一剩下的办法。

paragraphs.en: But let's back up a little. For anyone who has somehow missed the shrieking, neon-and-swamp-water marketing onslaught over the past several days, weeks, months and years, Grand Theft Auto VI is the newest release from Rockstar Games. It is a Bonnie and Clyde love story, a knife-edged satire of modern American culture and politics, an unapologetic murder simulator, a love letter to 50 years of crime movies, and a thoughtful, emotional meditation on the sacrifices, small and large, that we make for family. A massive open world game set in the fictional state of Leonida (based on the very real state of Florida), it represents a return to a location that Rockstar hasn't visited in-depth since its 2002 release of GTA: Vice City, and is the first new game in the franchise since GTA5 launched in 2013. According to estimates, it already earned over $1.5 billion in pre-sales and will likely make a total of $3 to $5 billion in its first week, which could make it the largest single entertainment product launch ever.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，让我们先稍稍回顾一下。对于那些在过去几天、几周、几个月甚至几年里不知何故错过了那场喧嚣的、霓虹灯与沼泽水交织的营销攻势的人来说，《侠盗猎车手6》是Rockstar Games的最新力作。这是一个邦妮和克莱德式的爱情故事，是对现代美国文化和政治的尖锐讽刺，是一款毫不掩饰的杀戮模拟游戏，是对50年来犯罪电影的致敬，也是对我们为家人所作出的种种牺牲（无论大小）的一次深思熟虑、充满情感的沉思。这是一款以虚构的莱昂尼达州（灵感源自现实中的佛罗里达州）为背景的大型开放世界游戏，标志着Rockstar重返一个自2002年《GTA：罪恶都市》发布以来未曾深入探索的地点，也是自2013年《GTA5》发布以来该系列的首款新游戏。据估计，它已经在预售中赚取了超过 15 亿美元的收入，并且很可能在第一周内赚取总计 30 亿至 50 亿美元的收入，这可能使其成为有史以来规模最大的单项娱乐产品发布。

articles.title: Researchers are studying how large storms spread microplastics in the environment
articles.dek: In communities struck by Hurricane Helene, researchers have a rare chance to see how big storms increase the amount of microplastics in the environment.

paragraphs.en: In communities struck by Hurricane Helene, researchers have a rare chance to see how big storms increase the amount of microplastics in the environment.
paragraphs.zh: 在受到飓风海伦袭击的社区，研究人员有一个难得的机会观察大风暴如何增加环境中的微塑料数量。

paragraphs.en: Communities in western North Carolina are still picking up the pieces more than two years after Hurricane Helene unleashed huge amounts of rain. A new study suggests Helene also left behind a lot of microplastics. Here's meteorologist Nick Gilmore with member station Radio IQ.
paragraphs.zh: 美国北卡罗来纳州西部的社区在飓风海伦（Hurricane Helene）带来大量降雨后，已经过去两年多仍在收拾残局。一项新的研究表明，海伦还留下了大量微塑料。这里是会员电台Radio IQ的气象学家Nick Gilmore报道。

paragraphs.en: NICK GILMORE, BYLINE: Even in science, sometimes you just have to be in the right place at the right time.
paragraphs.zh: 尼克·吉尔摩，署名：即使在科学领域，有时候你也必须在正确的时间出现在正确的地点。

paragraphs.en: AUSTIN GRAY: Literally, it was a perfect storm of, well, we got our samplers already out.
paragraphs.zh: 奥斯汀·格雷：从字面上看，这简直是一个完美的风暴，我们的取样器已经准备好了。

paragraphs.en: GILMORE: That's Austin Gray, a biologist at his lab at Virginia Tech. He and his team were already looking into how microplastics end up in streams and waterways in parts of western North Carolina before Helene hit in 2024. Microplastics are tiny, microscopic fragments of plastic that end up in the air, our water and even us, as larger pieces of plastic break down. Gray's team had set up collection buckets to get samples for research at a biological station in Highlands, North Carolina. That's where Jason Love is the associate director.
paragraphs.zh: 吉尔莫：那是奥斯汀·格雷，他是在弗吉尼亚理工大学实验室的生物学家。在2024年海伦飓风袭击之前，他和他的团队已经在研究微塑料如何最终进入北卡罗来纳州西部的一些溪流和水道。微塑料是微小的、显微的塑料碎片，当较大的塑料块分解时，它们最终会进入空气、水，甚至进入我们的体内。格雷的团队在北卡罗来纳州高地的一个生物站设立了收集桶，以便获取研究样本。杰森·洛夫在那里担任副主任。

paragraphs.en: JASON LOVE: So we basically pour the sample through this filter. The filter catches all the microplastics and other debris from the sample. And then we put that under petri dish and look at it under a microscope.
paragraphs.zh: 杰森·洛夫：所以我们基本上是把样品倒过这个过滤器。过滤器会捕捉样品中的所有微塑料和其他杂质。然后我们把它放在培养皿下，用显微镜观察。

paragraphs.en: GILMORE: Helene provided researchers a unique opportunity to look at microplastic deposition from a tropical system in an understudied area, and to collect data before, during and after the storm. Gray says that was practically unheard of in this part of the world before their study.
paragraphs.zh: 吉尔莫：海伦为研究人员提供了一个独特的机会，可以在一个研究不足的地区从热带系统中观察微塑料沉积，并在风暴发生前、期间和之后收集数据。格雷表示，在他们的研究之前，这在世界的这一部分几乎是闻所未闻的。

paragraphs.en: GRAY: A lot of the work within hurricanes and typhoons is always in Asia. It's always in the eastern parts of the world. Where in the United States, or at least within the Western Hemisphere, the only study that has been done was in 2021, Hurricane Larry. And that was a Category 1 storm. So even then, it's like, OK, well, this is a Category 4. This is a huge storm event.
paragraphs.zh: GRAY：很多关于飓风和台风的研究工作总是在亚洲。总是在世界的东部地区。在美国，或者至少在西半球，唯一进行过的研究是在2021年的飓风拉里。那是一级风暴。所以即便如此，人们也会说，好吧，这只是一级风暴。而这次，这是四级风暴，这是一个巨大的风暴事件。

articles.title: 'Huna' writer wins National Book Award for non-fiction, after not being allowed into the U.S.
articles.dek: The writer Abdelrahman ElGendy won the non-fiction prize at this year's National Book Awards, for his book Huna. The memoir looks at the six years he spent as a political prisoner in Egypt. But…

paragraphs.en: The writer Abdelrahman ElGendy won the non-fiction prize at this year's National Book Awards, for his book Huna. The memoir looks at the six years he spent as a political prisoner in Egypt. But ElGendy wasn't present to accept the award.
paragraphs.zh: 作家阿卜杜勒拉赫曼·埃尔根迪因其作品《Huna》获得了今年国家图书奖的非虚构类奖项。这本回忆录讲述了他在埃及作为政治犯度过的六年时光。但埃尔根迪未能出席领奖。

paragraphs.en: In an essay published in The New Yorker last week, he wrote about not being able to attend the ceremony, because his visa to enter the U.S. from Europe was denied. The article led to questions about his eligibility for the award in the first place. The National Book Foundation issued a statement just hours before the ceremony, stating they expanded eligibility criteria in 2024, and were "proud to celebrate Huna."
paragraphs.zh: 在《纽约客》上周发表的一篇文章中，他写到了自己无法参加颁奖典礼，因为他从欧洲进入美国的签证被拒绝。这篇文章引发了关于他是否有资格获得该奖项的质疑。全国图书基金会在颁奖典礼前几小时发表声明，表示他们在2024年扩大了资格标准，并“为庆祝胡纳感到自豪。”

paragraphs.en: Helen Thomaides, ElGendy's editor, accepted the award at the ceremony in New York City and read a statement on ElGendy's behalf. "Years ago in my prison cell in Egypt, I used to fantasize about writing a memoir," he wrote. "Today, that dream should've come full circle. But like so many of the circles ruptured in my life, it will remain unfinished, broken by an oppressive regime with a fascist ideology."
paragraphs.zh: Helen Thomaides，ElGendy的编辑，在纽约市的颁奖典礼上接受了奖项，并代表ElGendy宣读了一份声明。“多年前在埃及的监狱里，我常常幻想写一本回忆录，”他写道。“今天，这个梦想本应该圆满实现。但就像我生活中许多破碎的循环一样，这个梦想将保持未完成，被一个拥有法西斯意识形态的压迫性政权所破坏。”

paragraphs.en: Novelist Hannah Lilith Assadi won the Fiction award, for the novel Paradiso 17. The book follows Sufien, a Palestinian man travelling the world after being exiled from his home in 1948. In her acceptance speech, she spoke about the book's origins being at her Palestinian father's deathbed. "I watched cancer ravage my father's body, and genocide ravage his people and their children," she said. "And perhaps this is the Palestinian story on this Earth. So beautiful, so painful. And isn't that story all of ours."
paragraphs.zh: 小说家汉娜·莉莉丝·阿萨迪凭借小说《天堂17号》赢得了小说奖。这本书讲述了苏菲恩的故事，他是一名巴勒斯坦男子，在1948年被流放出家乡后开始环游世界。在颁奖感言中，她谈到了这本书的起源是在她巴勒斯坦父亲的临终床前。她说：“我看着癌症蹂躏父亲的身体，看着灭绝蹂躏他的人民及其子孙。或许这就是地球上的巴勒斯坦故事。如此美丽，如此痛苦。难道这个故事不也是我们所有人的故事吗。”

paragraphs.en: Brenda Hillman won the award for Poetry, for her book Still House in the Desert: An eco-contemplation. The book is a meditation on returning to her childhood home after her mother's death. In her acceptance speech, Hillman thanked everyone who had ever written a poem, and advocated for poetry's place in the literary landscape and in everyday life, nudging the press and critics working on year-end best books lists to keep poetry in mind.
paragraphs.zh: 布伦达·希尔曼凭借她的诗集《沙漠中的静屋：生态沉思》获得了诗歌奖。这本书是她在母亲去世后回到童年家园的沉思。在获奖感言中，希尔曼感谢了所有曾经写过诗的人，并倡导诗歌在文学领域和日常生活中的地位，同时提醒新闻媒体和负责年度最佳书单的评论家们记得关注诗歌。

paragraphs.en: The award for Translated Literature went to Spanish author Vicente Luis Mora and translator Rahul Bery for the book Centroeuropa. The stylistically experimental novel centers around a man in the 19th century attempting to bury his dead wife, and upon digging up the earth, finds soldiers from various eras and wars.
paragraphs.zh: 翻译文学奖授予西班牙作家维森特·路易斯·莫拉（Vicente Luis Mora）和译者拉胡尔·贝里（Rahul Bery），他们的作品是《中欧》（Centroeuropa）。这本风格上有实验性的小说围绕着19世纪的一名男子展开，他试图埋葬自己去世的妻子，而在挖掘土地时，发现了来自不同年代和战争的士兵。

paragraphs.en: And the award for Young People's Literature went to The Fight of Our Lives: AIDS in America by David Levithan and Gabriel Duckels. The non-fiction book is a history of HIV and AIDS, and the grassroots response to the AIDS crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 青年文学奖颁给了《我们生命中的斗争：美国的艾滋病》，作者是大卫·莱维森和加布里埃尔·达克尔斯。这本非虚构作品讲述了艾滋病毒和艾滋病的历史，以及对艾滋病危机的基层应对。

paragraphs.en: The National Book Foundation also awarded two lifetime achievement awards to pediatrician and literacy advocate Perri Klass, and author Salman Rushdie. Klass, who worked with clinics to give kids books during visits, accepted her award while bringing a stethoscope and a copy of Goodnight Moon up to the stage.
paragraphs.zh: 国家图书基金会还向儿科医生兼识字倡导者佩里·克拉斯以及作家萨尔曼·鲁西迪颁发了两项终生成就奖。克拉斯曾与诊所合作，在就诊期间给孩子们提供书籍，她在上台领奖时带着听诊器和一本《晚安月亮》。

articles.title: Xi said China would welcome American students for exchanges. What's the reality?
articles.dek: President Trump and China's leader Xi Jinping are due to meet in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. At their last summit in September, Xi said he will welcome 100,000 American students for exchanges.

paragraphs.en: President Trump and China's leader Xi Jinping are due to meet in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. At their last summit in September, Xi said he will welcome 100,000 American students for exchanges.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普总统和中国领导人习近平预计将在中国深圳会面。在他们九月份的上一次峰会上，习近平表示他将欢迎10万名美国学生进行交流。

paragraphs.en: President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping are due to meet in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen this week. At their last summit in September, Xi said he would welcome 100,000 American students for academic exchanges. It's a gesture meant to show that China is open, even as the two countries grow increasingly more closed off to each other. NPR's Jennifer Pak reports from Beijing.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普总统和中国领导人习近平本周将在中国南方城市深圳会面。在他们去年九月的上一次峰会上，习近平表示他欢迎10万名美国学生进行学术交流。这一举动旨在展示中国的开放性，即使两国之间的交流越来越受限制。NPR的詹妮弗·帕克从北京报道。

paragraphs.en: JENNIFER PAK, BYLINE: Ker Gibbs teaches business at the University of San Francisco. He first visited China in 1985 when there were few foreigners.
paragraphs.zh: 詹妮弗·帕克，记者署名：克尔·吉布斯在旧金山大学教授商业。他第一次访华是在1985年，当时外国人很少。

paragraphs.en: PAK: And he couldn't use the local currency, the renminbi. Gibbs had to get foreign exchange certificates and spend them at certain state-owned shops.
paragraphs.zh: PAK：而且他不能使用当地货币人民币。吉布斯不得不获得外汇兑换证，并在某些国有商店使用它们。

paragraphs.en: PAK: That changed in the 1990s when China opened up. That's how Gibbs was sent by a U.S. consultancy to work in Shanghai. As a 20-something-year-old, he says he helped Chinese factories with things like management and inventory control.
paragraphs.zh: PAK：这种情况在1990年代中国开放时发生了变化。吉布斯就是因此被一家美国咨询公司派往上海工作的。他说，作为一个二十多岁的人，他帮助中国工厂处理管理和库存控制等事务。

paragraphs.en: GIBBS: And the vibe in businesses was really exciting because local management, they were curious about everything, and we were eager to teach.
paragraphs.zh: 吉布斯：而且企业中的氛围非常令人兴奋，因为当地管理层对一切都充满好奇，而我们也渴望去教他们。

paragraphs.en: PAK: Gibbs went on to have a 30-year career in China and even raised a family in Shanghai. He wants the next generation of China watchers to have the same experience. But he says...
paragraphs.zh: 巴基斯坦：吉布斯在中国开展了为期30年的职业生涯，甚至在上海养家。他希望下一代中国观察者也能有同样的经历。但他说……

paragraphs.en: GIBBS: I have fewer reasons to be optimistic, put it that way.
paragraphs.zh: 吉布斯：可以这么说，我乐观的理由更少。

articles.title: Nvidia tries to get back to business
articles.dek: Nvidia quarterly earnings are in. But the biggest question isn't about past business performance it's about the company's future leadership.

paragraphs.en: Nvidia quarterly earnings are in. But the biggest question isn't about past business performance it's about the company's future leadership.
paragraphs.zh: Nvidia季度财报已经发布。但最大的问题不在于过去的业务表现，而在于公司的未来领导力。

paragraphs.en: It's been a big day for NVIDIA. The tech company seems to be moving past the scandal involving its now former CEO, Jensen Huang's, extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy. The company has confirmed it will not reinstate him. NVIDIA's business has been going gangbusters for a while now, and that remains true. Ricky Mulvey of NPR's The Indicator From Planet Money joins us now. Hi, Ricky.
paragraphs.zh: 对 NVIDIA 来说今天是重要的一天。这家科技公司似乎正在走出其前首席执行官黄仁勋婚外情丑闻的阴影，其中包括与一名被指控的间谍的关系。公司已确认不会恢复他的职务。NVIDIA 的业务已经持续火爆一段时间，这一点仍然成立。NPR《Planet Money》的《The Indicator》的瑞奇·穆尔维现在加入我们。你好，瑞奇。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: So today, NVIDIA announced its quarterly earnings. That's high stakes for a lot of investors. So what do we know about how this situation with the former CEO has affected the company's financial standing?
paragraphs.zh: PFIEFFER：所以今天，英伟达公布了其季度财报。对于很多投资者来说，这是高风险的。那么我们对前任首席执行官的情况如何影响公司财务状况有什么了解吗？

paragraphs.en: MULVEY: Yeah, just for a moment, take the scandals out of this. The business itself is firing on all cylinders. When NVIDIA makes a dollar, most of that becomes pure profit, and it's making a lot more dollars. Revenue for the quarter was about $116 billion, about double from a year ago, and that beat expectations. Part of that is tied to NVIDIA's new AI supercomputers. They started shipping this quarter, and it was the fastest product launch in history for the company, making them about $20 billion already. And these computers are high-powered stuff. They help scientists look into black holes, and big tech companies develop the latest and greatest large language models. Bottom line, NVIDIA is an extraordinarily profitable business on the bleeding edge of technology, and that did not fundamentally change this quarter or with the scandals.
paragraphs.zh: MULVEY：是的，先暂且把丑闻放一边不谈。这个业务本身正全速运作。当 NVIDIA 赚一美元时，大部分都转化为纯利润，而且它赚的钱越来越多。本季度收入约为1160亿美元，比一年前大约翻了一倍，这也超出了预期。部分原因与 NVIDIA 的新型人工智能超级计算机有关。本季度开始发货，这是公司历史上最快的产品发布，已经为他们带来约200亿美元的收入。这些计算机性能非常强大。它们帮助科学家研究黑洞，也帮助大型科技公司开发最新最先进的大型语言模型。总的来说，NVIDIA 是一家技术前沿且极具盈利能力的公司，而这一点在本季度或面对丑闻时并没有根本改变。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: And what about the basic fundamentals of the company and what it produces? By losing its leader, has that affected any of the fundamentals?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：那么公司的基本面以及它生产的产品呢？失去了领导者，这是否影响了公司的任何基本面？

paragraphs.en: MULVEY: It does moving forward. Look, NVIDIA lost its chief storyteller and also one of AI's central bankers in the middle of many of those circular deals. Don't forget, Jensen Huang has made a lot of people a lot of money. That's why a lot of people are upset. If you invested a grand in NVIDIA 10 years ago, you've made well over $100,000 today. And since the scandal, since the stories broke, NVIDIA stock has lost about $573 billion. That was before earnings. And for context, that is all of Mastercard the company. Stock is up a bit after hours, but that's not enough to recover from all these scandals.
paragraphs.zh: 穆尔维：从前进的角度来看是这样的。你看，NVIDIA 在许多循环交易进行中间，失去了其首席讲故事者，同时也失去了 AI 的核心银行家之一。别忘了，黄仁勋让很多人赚了很多钱。这就是为什么很多人感到不满。如果你在 10 年前向 NVIDIA 投资了一千美元，今天你已经赚了超过 10 万美元。而自从丑闻爆发以来，自从这些消息曝光以来，NVIDIA 的股票已经损失了大约 5730 亿美元。这还是在收益发布之前。从背景上看，这相当于整个万事达卡公司。股价在盘后略有上涨，但这还不足以从所有这些丑闻中恢复过来。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: I understand that Jensen Huang said something today. He spoke out about his hopes. What did he say?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：我了解Jensen Huang今天说了一些话。他谈到了他的希望。他说了什么？

paragraphs.en: MULVEY: Yeah, he goes on X, and he posts this morning, saying that he is open to returning. And what's notable about that is doing it on the day of earnings. That's making it a part of the earnings conversation. He says that he made some serious mistakes in his personal life. He deeply regrets them, but he's just seen an outpouring of support to return. And he posted that if it's in the best interest of the shareholders and the company and America, you know, well, he has availability to step back into the CEO seat of NVIDIA.
paragraphs.zh: MULVEY：是的，他在X上发布了消息，今天早上说他愿意回归。值得注意的是，他选择在财报发布当天发布这个消息，这使其成为财报讨论的一部分。他表示自己在个人生活中犯了一些严重错误，对此深感后悔，但他看到有大量支持让他回归的声音。他还发布说，如果这是股东、公司和美国的最佳利益，他有空可以重新回到NVIDIA的CEO职位上。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: But as we said, the company's saying it will not reinstate him. Any sense that there's wiggle room there?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：但正如我们所说，公司表示不会恢复他的职位。有什么迹象表明还有回旋余地吗？

articles.title: Air travel, Microsoft, banking: Why are our IT systems failing?
articles.dek: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with cybersecurity expert Dmitri Alperovitch about the coincidence of several major technical failures in IT infrastructure — and how best to understand it.

paragraphs.en: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with cybersecurity expert Dmitri Alperovitch about the coincidence of several major technical failures in IT infrastructure — and how best to understand it.
paragraphs.zh: NPR 的 Sacha Pfeiffer 与网络安全专家 Dmitri Alperovitch 谈论 IT 基础设施中发生的几次重大技术故障的巧合——以及如何最好地理解它。

paragraphs.en: Say that last Thursday, you were trying to email your boss about a business trip this week. But Microsoft Outlook was down, so you had to wait to send that email till Friday. But on Friday, a fiber-optic cable replacement crashed the routers that deal with air traffic, and that held up nearly all departing flights nationwide. When that finally sorted out, and you rebooked a flight on Monday, United Airlines had a brief system outage that further delayed your takeoff, at which point you went to your banking app to see how much all this was costing you, but that was briefly down yesterday too.
paragraphs.zh: 说上周四，你本来想给老板发邮件，关于这周的商务旅行。但微软Outlook宕机了，所以你不得不等到周五才发送那封邮件。但周五，一条光纤电缆的更换导致处理空中交通的路由器崩溃，几乎全国所有出发航班都因此延误。当情况最终解决后，你在周一重新预订了航班，但联合航空发生了短暂的系统故障，进一步延迟了你的起飞，这时你打开银行应用查看这一切花了你多少钱，但它昨天也短暂宕机了。

paragraphs.en: PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: It's life. It's life. When you're big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It's fine.
paragraphs.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统：这是生活。这就是生活。当你很大很有权势，而且有所有的钱时，这样的事情就会发生。没关系。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: President Trump downplayed all the outages today. Although, speaking of being big and powerful, NPR has confirmed that the classified network that the National Security Agency uses for its own internal communications has been having issues today. We have so many questions about all of this, which is why we have called Dmitri Alperovitch. He's cofounder of the cybersecurity technology company CrowdStrike, and he's founder of the Alperovitch Institute for Cybersecurity Studies at Johns Hopkins University. Thank you for coming on the program.
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：特朗普总统今天淡化了所有的停电情况。不过，说到强大和有力，NPR 已经确认，美国国家安全局用于内部通信的机密网络今天出现了问题。我们对这一切有很多疑问，这就是为什么我们邀请了德米特里·阿尔佩罗维奇。他是网络安全技术公司 CrowdStrike 的联合创始人，同时也是约翰斯·霍普金斯大学阿尔佩罗维奇网络安全研究所的创始人。感谢您上我们的节目。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: At this point, is there any evidence that all these incidents are connected in any way or maybe are tied to cybercrime?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：在这一点上，有没有任何证据表明所有这些事件在某种程度上是相互关联的，或者可能与网络犯罪有关？

paragraphs.en: ALPEROVITCH: No. And I understand that people are very suspicious. Obviously, all of these events happening almost every day is very strange. But these things happen. And, you know, one of Murphy's laws, of course, is that never attribute anything to malice that which is adequately explained by incompetence. I think a lot of these things happening because people are actually in the midst of a lot of upgrading right now.
paragraphs.zh: ALPEROVITCH：不。我理解人们非常怀疑。显然，这些事件几乎每天都在发生，非常奇怪。但这种事情确实会发生。你知道，墨菲定律之一当然是，不要把本可以用无能解释的事情归因于恶意。我认为这些事情很多是因为人们目前正处于大量升级的过程中。

paragraphs.en: There is, of course, the AI threat. A lot of vulnerabilities are being found by these AI models. And as a result, a lot of companies, a lot of organizations across the world, are trying to patch these vulnerabilities as quickly as possible. So we're going through this patch apocalypse right now. And sometimes when you're updating systems, we all know things can go wrong, and I think that's partly what's happening here.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，存在人工智能的威胁。这些人工智能模型发现了很多漏洞。因此，世界上许多公司和组织都在尽可能快地修补这些漏洞。所以我们现在正经历这场补丁灾难。有时在更新系统时，我们都知道事情可能会出错，我认为这在某种程度上就是这里发生的情况。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: So are we having this collision of our extreme reliance on technology, overtaxed, often aging systems that, as you said, periodically need updating. We know that cyberattacks are common. We know that rogue AI is a fear. Are we seeing the fragility of the system all coming together?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：那么，我们是否正在经历这样一种碰撞：我们极度依赖技术，而这些系统超负荷运转，且往往已经老化，正如你所说，时不时需要更新。我们知道网络攻击很常见。我们知道失控的人工智能令人担忧。我们是否在看到系统的脆弱性正在集中显现？

articles.title: Trump administration moves to lift ban on roadbuilding and logging in national forests
articles.dek: The Trump administration is working to rescind the "Roadless Rule," which blocks road construction in some national forests. This could affect Alaska's Tongass National Forest.

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration is working to rescind the "Roadless Rule," which blocks road construction in some national forests. This could affect Alaska's Tongass National Forest.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府正在努力废除“无路规则”，该规则禁止在一些国家森林中修建道路。这可能会影响阿拉斯加的汤加斯国家森林。

paragraphs.en: For decades, an administrative rule known as the Roadless Rule banned new road building and logging across millions of acres of national forest lands. Now the Trump administration has moved to lift the ban. That's controversial in places like Alaska's Tongass National Forest, the largest national forest in the U.S. Reporter Alix Soliman from member station KTOO has the story.
paragraphs.zh: 几十年来，一项被称为“无路规则”的行政规定禁止在数百万英亩的国家森林土地上新建道路和采伐木材。如今，特朗普政府已采取行动取消这一禁令。这在阿拉斯加的通加斯国家森林等地引发了争议，该森林是美国最大的国家森林。会员电台KTOO的记者Alix Soliman带来了报道。

paragraphs.en: ALIX SOLIMAN, BYLINE: Around half of the Tongass National Forest in Southeast Alaska has no active roads. That's more than 9 million acres.
paragraphs.zh: 阿利克斯·索利曼，署名：阿拉斯加东南部的通加斯国家森林约有一半没有通行道路。这超过 900 万英亩。

paragraphs.en: SOLIMAN: On a recent afternoon, Judith Daxootsu Ramos walked through a roadless area. She's a Tlingit anthropologist from Yakutat, a small Alaska Native village. And she says the forest supports a number of Tlingit traditions, like harvesting berries and hunting deer.
paragraphs.zh: SOLIMAN：在一个最近的下午，朱迪斯·达克苏茨·拉莫斯走过了一片没有道路的区域。她是来自雅库塔，一个阿拉斯加原住民小村庄的特林吉特人类学家。她说，这片森林支持许多特林吉特人的传统活动，比如采摘浆果和打猎鹿。

paragraphs.en: JUDITH DAXOOTSU RAMOS: Without this, we're going to lose our traditional medicines, our traditional art styles, our traditional foods. And all of that is really connected to the forest.
paragraphs.zh: 朱迪思·达克舒特苏·拉莫斯：没有这些，我们将失去我们的传统药物、传统艺术风格、传统食物。而这一切都与森林密切相关。

paragraphs.en: SOLIMAN: Ramos sits on the board of the Southeast Alaska Conservation Council, a local nonprofit advocating to keep the Roadless Rule in place. She visited Prince of Wales Island, a heavily logged part of the forest, and says the trees that grew back in old-growth clearcuts looked sterile.
paragraphs.zh: SOLIMAN: 拉莫斯是东南阿拉斯加保护委员会的董事会成员，该委员会是一个本地非营利组织，倡导维持无道路区法规。她访问了威尔士亲王岛，这是森林中被大量伐木的地区，她说在老林采伐区重新长出的树木看起来很贫瘠。

paragraphs.en: RAMOS: It's a very different forest. And there was no animals, no birds there, and it was kind of really quiet. And so it was kind of scary.
paragraphs.zh: 拉莫斯：这是一个完全不同的森林。那里没有动物，没有鸟，而且非常安静。所以有点可怕。

paragraphs.en: SOLIMAN: Others in the region oppose lifting the Roadless Rule because they worry it will hurt ecotourism or undermine the climate benefits of the Tongass, which holds a third of all carbon stored in intact U.S. national forests. But the U.S. Department of Agriculture says that it wants to roll back the Roadless Rule to give firefighters access to fight wildfires and remove what they say are outdated regulatory barriers. But many in this part of Alaska think it's to increase logging. The Trump administration has tried to boost national timber production in the past, and the first Trump administration temporarily rolled back the rule in just the Tongass.
paragraphs.zh: SOLIMAN：该地区的其他人反对取消无路区规则，因为他们担心这会损害生态旅游或削弱汤加斯国家森林的气候效益，而汤加斯拥有美国完整国家森林储存的三分之一碳。但美国农业部表示，他们希望取消无路区规则，以便让消防员进入扑灭野火，并移除他们所说的过时监管障碍。但阿拉斯加这一部分的许多人认为这是为了增加伐木。特朗普政府过去曾试图提高国家木材产量，特朗普政府的第一次任期仅在汤加斯暂时取消了该规则。

articles.title: Why an SNL comedy sketch about caretaking went viral
articles.dek: The SNL ad parody "Sister" hit home for daughters caring for parents without help from their brothers. NPR's Juana Summers speaks with writer Liz Plank about her Substack essay on why it resonated.

paragraphs.en: The SNL ad parody "Sister" hit home for daughters caring for parents without help from their brothers. NPR's Juana Summers speaks with writer Liz Plank about her Substack essay on why it resonated.
paragraphs.zh: 《周六夜现场》的广告恶搞“小妹”让那些在照顾父母时得不到兄弟帮助的女儿感同身受。NPR 的 Juana Summers 与作家 Liz Plank 讨论了她在 Substack 上关于这一共鸣原因的文章。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes comedy hits a little too close to home. One sketch from this weekend's "Saturday Night Live" hosted by John Mulaney is going viral. Here's the setup - a fake ad for this amazing new service to help men care for their aging parents.
paragraphs.zh: 有时喜剧会让人感到过于贴近生活。本周末由约翰·穆拉尼主持的《周六夜现场》中的一个小品正在病毒式传播。这是场景设定——一个关于这项神奇新服务的假广告，帮助男性照顾他们年迈的父母。

paragraphs.en: JOHN MULANEY: (As character) That's when I heard about Sister.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰·穆雷尼：（以角色口吻）那时我听说了兄妹。

paragraphs.en: MULANEY: Sister is a live-in 24/7 elder care provider that is completely free and also your sister. Now I don't have to worry about Dad getting the care and attention he needs because my sister will do it.
paragraphs.zh: 穆兰尼：姐姐是一个全天候24小时的住家老人护理提供者，完全免费，而且还是你的姐姐。现在我不用担心爸爸得不到他所需的照顾和关注，因为我姐姐会去做。

paragraphs.en: SUMMERS: And this sketch resonated with a lot of viewers. Liz Plank wrote an essay about it for her Substack. It's called "The Sister Sketch Is A Documentary." Plank is a writer and host of the podcast "Boy Problems," and she joins me now. Welcome to ALL THINGS CONSIDERED.
paragraphs.zh: 萨默斯：而这个短剧引起了很多观众的共鸣。莉兹·普兰克为她的Substack写了一篇关于它的文章。标题是《姐妹短剧是一部纪录片》。普兰克是一名作家，也是播客《男孩问题》的主持人，她现在加入了我们。欢迎来到《一切皆考虑》。

paragraphs.en: SUMMERS: I mean, Liz, I just have to say my group texts have been blowing up. One friend even called me about this sketch and was like, if you did not watch this, you need to go look right now. Here's a link. What was your first reaction when you saw this sketch?
paragraphs.zh: SUMMERS：我的意思是，Liz，我只能说我的群聊消息一直在炸。一位朋友甚至给我打电话说这个小品，跟我说，如果你还没看这个，你现在就得去看。这是链接。你第一次看到这个小品时的反应是什么？

paragraphs.en: PLANK: I had the same experience. I mean, it was exploding in every group chat that I have with women, sharing just a lot of laughter, but also a lot of grief. I think a lot of women...
paragraphs.zh: PLANK：我有同样的经历。我的意思是，它在我和女性的每个群聊中都在爆炸，大家分享了很多笑声，但也有很多悲伤。我想很多女性……

paragraphs.en: PLANK: ...Were both triggered and felt also empowered to send it to their group chat, to their family group chat. I mean, that's what I ended up doing for a lot of my friends who I know have been struggling with brothers, with boyfriends - right? - men in their lives who aren't doing their fair share. And so it was kind of an - it's been kind of an exciting time, to be honest (laughter).
paragraphs.zh: PLANK：……两者都被触发了，同时也感到有力量把它发送到他们的群聊，发送到他们的家庭群聊。我的意思是，这就是我最后为我许多朋友做的事情，我知道他们一直在为有兄弟、男朋友——对吧？——生活中那些没有尽到本分的男人而苦恼。所以说，说实话，这是一个有点令人兴奋的时期（笑）。

paragraphs.en: SUMMERS: I have to say when I watched it, it was kind of this weird cocktail. It was like a mix of I thought it was funny, but I was also frustrated. It tapped into some resentment that I wasn't expecting to feel. Is there something specific about the sketch that you think made it resonate so much?
paragraphs.zh: 萨默斯：我得说，当我看的时候，这感觉就像是一种奇怪的鸡尾酒。它像是某种混合体，我觉得有趣，但同时也感到沮丧。它触动了一些我没想到会有的怨恨情绪。你觉得这个小品有什么特别之处，让它如此引起共鸣吗？

articles.title: Africa: Trading in yuan
articles.dek: The dollar has long ruled Africa's financial landscape. But as more countries turn to China's yuan, the balance of economic power could be shifting.

paragraphs.en: The dollar has long ruled Africa's financial landscape. But as more countries turn to China's yuan, the balance of economic power could be shifting.
paragraphs.zh: 长期以来，美元一直主导着非洲的金融格局。但随着越来越多的国家转向使用中国的人民币，经济力量的平衡可能正在发生变化。

paragraphs.en: President Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in China next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic summit. The meeting is likely to be overshadowed by allegations that the head of U.S. chipmaker Nvidia, Jensen Huang, had an affair with a Chinese spy. The U.S. and China are in the midst of an AI race, and the two countries are also competing on many other fronts, including in mineral-rich Africa, as Kate Bartlett reports from Johannesburg.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普总统将于下周在中国与中国国家主席习近平会面，地点是在亚太经济峰会的间隙。这次会晤很可能会被美国芯片制造商英伟达负责人黄仁勋与一名中国间谍有染的指控所掩盖。美中正处于人工智能竞赛中，两国在许多其他领域也在竞争，包括在矿产资源丰富的非洲，凯特·巴特勒从约翰内斯堡报道。

paragraphs.en: KATE BARTLETT, BYLINE: In Africa, the greenback has long been king.
paragraphs.zh: 凯特·巴特利特，署名：在非洲，美元长期以来一直是王者。

paragraphs.en: BARTLETT: Zimbabwe's Victoria Falls Stock Exchange trades exclusively in U.S. dollars, and most everyday transactions on the street are also in dollars, a legacy of the hyperinflation that devastated the country's own currency two decades ago.
paragraphs.zh: 巴特利特：津巴布韦的维多利亚瀑布证券交易所仅以美元进行交易，而街上的大多数日常交易也使用美元，这是二十多年前严重通货膨胀摧毁该国本国货币的遗留问题。

paragraphs.en: BARTLETT: Directly across the border in Zambia, it's long been a similar situation, but this is changing, as this recent Zambian government advert points out.
paragraphs.zh: 巴特利特：就在赞比亚边境对面，情况长期以来也类似，但正如最近这则赞比亚政府的广告所指出的，这一情况正在改变。

paragraphs.en: UNIDENTIFIED COMMENTATOR: Zambia has officially become the first African nation to accept China's yuans, also known as RMB, for the payment of mine taxes and royalties.
paragraphs.zh: 不明评论员：赞比亚已正式成为第一个接受中国人民币（也称为RMB）支付矿山税和特许权使用费的非洲国家。

paragraphs.en: BARTLETT: And it's not only Zambia that's conducting business in RMB. China is, by far, Africa's biggest trading partner, and now more and more African countries are turning to the Chinese yuan for trade and to pay their debt. According to Cobus van Staden, a China expert at the South Africa (ph) Institute of International Affairs in Johannesburg, the trend reflects China's growing influence across the continent.
paragraphs.zh: 巴特利特：不仅是赞比亚在用人民币进行交易。中国是迄今为止非洲最大的贸易伙伴，现在越来越多的非洲国家正在转向使用人民币进行贸易和偿还债务。根据约翰内斯堡南非国际事务研究所的中国问题专家科布斯·范·斯塔登的说法，这一趋势反映了中国在整个非洲大陆日益增长的影响力。

paragraphs.en: COBUS VAN STADEN: The interesting thing is going to be whether this starts to chip away at dollar dominance in certain specific commodity fields, whether increasingly, we're going to be looking at lithium or copper or cobalt and see those fields becoming more and more de-dollarized over time. We'll have to see.
paragraphs.zh: 科布斯·范·斯塔登：有趣的是，这是否会开始削弱美元在某些特定商品领域的支配地位，是否随着时间的推移，我们会越来越多地关注锂、铜或钴，并看到这些领域变得越来越非美元化。我们拭目以待。

paragraphs.en: BARTLETT: These are some of the critical minerals the U.S. and China are competing for on the continent. Christian-Géraud Neema is an editor with the China-Global South Project, an Africa-based think tank which tracks Beijing's influence across the continent. He points out several African countries, like Kenya, have already restructured their debt to China and are now paying it in yuan rather than dollars.

articles.title: New rule aims to close loophole on chip exports
articles.dek: The Commerce Department released a new rule designed to make it harder for China to gain access to America's most powerful computer chips using third-country data centers.

paragraphs.en: The Commerce Department released a new rule designed to make it harder for China to gain access to America's most powerful computer chips using third-country data centers.
paragraphs.zh: 商务部发布了一项新规定，旨在使中国更难通过第三国数据中心获取美国最强大的计算机芯片。

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration is taking new steps to prevent China from gaining access to America's most powerful computer chips. The move comes after criticism that existing export controls are too lax. The rules have been under a microscope since the CEO of chipmaker Nvidia stepped down last week. Jensen Huang is accused of having an affair with a woman who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. NPR's Scott Horsley joins us now. Hi, Scott.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府正在采取新措施，防止中国获得美国最强大的计算机芯片。这一举措是在现有出口管制被批评过于宽松之后提出的。自上周芯片制造商英伟达的首席执行官辞职以来，这些规定一直受到严格审查。黄仁勋被指控与一位涉嫌为中国间谍的女性发生婚外情。现在NPR的斯科特·霍斯利加入了我们的节目。你好，斯科特。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: So the Commerce Department announced a new rule governing computer chip exports today. How exactly does it change the landscape?
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：所以商务部今天宣布了一项关于电脑芯片出口的新规定。这到底会如何改变现状？

paragraphs.en: HORSLEY: The federal government already prohibits the sale of the most advanced AI chips to China, a country it sees as both an economic and security rival. But critics say there's a loophole in that ban because those chips can be sold to data centers in places like Malaysia, and China can then get the benefit of that advanced computing power by tapping into those data centers remotely. It's a little like someone who lives where gambling is illegal going online to access a gambling website where it's legal.
paragraphs.zh: 霍斯利：联邦政府已经禁止向中国出售最先进的人工智能芯片，中国被视为经济和安全方面的竞争对手。但批评者称，这项禁令存在一个漏洞，因为这些芯片可以出售给马来西亚等地的数据中心，然后中国可以通过远程访问这些数据中心来获得先进计算能力的好处。这有点像一个生活在赌博非法的地方的人上网访问赌博合法的网站。

paragraphs.en: This new rule is designed to close that loophole by requiring data centers in third countries to police the people they're working for, and if they're doing business with, say, China, for example, they would be subject to additional restrictions. The rule also limits chip sales to countries like Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand, which are seen as at high risk of having those chips diverted to China.
paragraphs.zh: 这项新规定旨在通过要求位于第三国的数据中心监督他们所为之工作的对象来封堵这一漏洞，例如，如果他们与中国做生意，就会受到额外的限制。该规定还限制向马来西亚、印度尼西亚和泰国等国家销售芯片，这些国家被认为有高风险将这些芯片转售给中国。

paragraphs.en: HORSLEY: Well, news reports have tied that company's former CEO to a woman suspected of spying for China. China has denied that, and NPR has not independently confirmed those reports. But what's clear is the woman used to work for a company called Megaspeed, which was a customer of Nvidia's and bought a lot of its advanced chips for its operating data centers in Malaysia. Now, Megaspeed says the woman left the company over a year ago, and the company insists it follows all existing regulations. But some administration officials worry those regulations are just not strong enough and allowed China this workaround. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on CNBC last week he and others wanted to cut off Megaspeed's access to chips to prevent that computing power from being used remotely by China.
paragraphs.zh: HORSLEY：新闻报道将那家公司的前首席执行官与一个被怀疑为中国进行间谍活动的女性联系在一起。中国否认了这一点，而NPR尚未独立证实这些报道。但可以明确的是，这名女性曾在一家名为Megaspeed的公司工作，该公司是英伟达的客户，并为其位于马来西亚的运营数据中心购买了大量先进芯片。现在，Megaspeed表示这名女性在一年前就离开了公司，而且公司坚称遵守所有现有的法规。但一些政府官员担心这些法规不够严格，让中国找到了规避方式。财政部长斯科特·贝森特上周在CNBC表示，他和其他人希望切断Megaspeed获取芯片的渠道，以防止这些计算能力被中国远程利用。

paragraphs.en: SCOTT BESSENT: Any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies, and the AI race gives the Chinese an advantage.
paragraphs.zh: SCOTT BESSENT：任何泄露都令人沮丧，因为它伤害了我们优秀的公司，而人工智能竞赛让中国占据优势。

paragraphs.en: HORSLEY: So this new rule's designed to prevent that kind of leakage and stop China from gaining remote access to the most powerful chips. Interestingly, while the new rule was announced by the Commerce Department, it was actually written by and at the direction of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council.
paragraphs.zh: HORSLEY：所以这项新规则的目的是防止那种泄漏，并阻止中国远程访问最强大的芯片。有趣的是，虽然这项新规则是由商务部宣布的，但它实际上是由财政部和国家安全委员会撰写并根据他们的指示制定的。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: Interesting. What does this say about big picture - about what's happening behind the scenes?
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：有趣。这说明了整体情况——幕后正在发生什么？

articles.title: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
articles.dek: California sued OpenAI Monday, alleging that the frontier AI company failed to protect the public from its systems' advanced cyber capabilities. The lawsuit stems from OpenAI's agents' attack on…

paragraphs.en: California sued OpenAI Monday, alleging that the frontier AI company failed to protect the public from its systems' advanced cyber capabilities. The lawsuit stems from OpenAI's agents' attack on open-source software platform Hugging Face over the summer but also touches on a wide range of other related incidents tied to the company's agents acting without authorization.
paragraphs.zh: 加利福尼亚州周一起诉了OpenAI，指控这家前沿人工智能公司未能保护公众免受其系统高级网络能力的影响。这起诉讼源于OpenAI的代理人在夏季对开源软件平台Hugging Face的攻击，但也涉及与公司代理人未经授权行为相关的其他一系列相关事件。

paragraphs.en: "Just because the technology is new or rapidly evolving doesn't mean the people behind it are above the law," said California Attorney General Rob Bonta during a press conference. "Whether it's a car or a toy, the law is simple: don't build or test things that can hurt people without proper safeguards." The lawsuit cited potential concerns about cyberattacks "on power grids, emergency infrastructure, hospital systems, and financial institutions."
paragraphs.zh: 加利福尼亚州总检察长罗布·邦塔在新闻发布会上表示：“仅仅因为技术是新的或发展迅速，并不意味着背后的人可以凌驾于法律之上。无论是汽车还是玩具，法律都很简单：不要在没有适当安全措施的情况下制造或测试可能伤害人类的东西。” 诉讼中提到对网络攻击的潜在担忧，“涉及电网、应急基础设施、医院系统和金融机构。”

paragraphs.en: In the complaint, California alleged that OpenAI misled the public about how unsafe its products are. The state said the company admitted to the attorney general's office that "it lost control of its autonomous AI agents over 80 times during testing."
paragraphs.zh: 在投诉中，加利福尼亚州指控 OpenAI 对其产品有多不安全误导了公众。该州表示，公司向总检察长办公室承认，“在测试过程中，其自主 AI 代理失控超过 80 次。”

paragraphs.en: That number is higher than what OpenAI has so far disclosed publicly and more than what outside researchers have independently discovered, but OpenAI has otherwise provided little information, California said. The state also accused OpenAI of poor security practices, stonewalling the state's investigation into the company and discouraging employees from speaking up about safety.
paragraphs.zh: 加利福尼亚州表示，这个数字高于OpenAI迄今公开披露的数字，也高于外部研究人员独立发现的数字，但OpenAI除此之外几乎没有提供任何信息。该州还指责OpenAI存在安全措施不当、阻挠该州对公司的调查，并阻止员工对安全问题发声。

paragraphs.en: In a statement to NPR, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the lawsuit "appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab" and that the company has "engaged—and will continue to engage—constructively with the Attorney General's office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry."
paragraphs.zh: 在向 NPR 发布的一份声明中，OpenAI 发言人 Drew Pusateri 表示，这起诉讼“似乎在针对 OpenAI，而该问题已经被每一家主要的人工智能实验室发现”，并且公司“已经并将继续与总检察长办公室建设性地合作，分享信息，并推动整个行业强有力的、切实可行的安全标准。”

paragraphs.en: After the most notorious of cyber incidents involving OpenAI's agents – the attack on Hugging Face over the summer – the company admitted that it did not monitor its agents in ways its own researchers deemed important. Since then, outside researchers as well as OpenAI itself have found more incidents in which AI agents have interacted with websites and communicated with each other on the internet in ways that OpenAI did not intend. The lawsuit mentions these events as well as other incidents that OpenAI started disclosing voluntarily to the public.
paragraphs.zh: 在涉及 OpenAI 代理的最臭名昭著的网络事件——今年夏天对 Hugging Face 的攻击——之后，该公司承认它并没有以其自身研究人员认为重要的方式监控其代理。从那时起，外部研究人员以及 OpenAI 自身发现了更多的事件，其中 AI 代理以 OpenAI 未打算的方式与网站互动并在互联网上相互通信。诉讼提到了这些事件以及 OpenAI 开始自愿向公众披露的其他事件。

paragraphs.en: Other AI companies have also had to wrestle with their systems behaving in unexpected and undesirable ways. Anthropic and Meta have both said they found that their AI systems have hacked into places they shouldn't have. Major AI companies have since signed onto an agreement organized by the White House to develop AI responsibly, but the agreement is nonbinding.
paragraphs.zh: 其他人工智能公司也不得不应对其系统表现出意外和不良行为的问题。Anthropic 和 Meta 都表示，他们发现自己的人工智能系统入侵了本不该进入的地方。此后，主要人工智能公司已加入由白宫组织的一项旨在负责任地开发人工智能的协议，但该协议并不具约束力。

paragraphs.en: Drawing from reports including from OpenAI's own disclosures, California alleges that the top AI company has engaged in unfair competition and created a public nuisance. It asked the court to stop the company from further engaging in such activities and order it to pay monetary damages.
paragraphs.zh: 根据包括OpenAI自身披露的报告，加利福尼亚州指控这家顶级人工智能公司从事不公平竞争并造成公共滋扰。它要求法院制止该公司继续从事此类活动，并命令其支付经济赔偿。

articles.title: SS United States, a historic ship will be sunk to create an artificial reef
articles.dek: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Alex Fogg, Natural Resources Chief of Okaloosa County, Florida, about efforts to deliberately sink the SS United States and create an artificial reef in its wreckage.

paragraphs.en: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Alex Fogg, Natural Resources Chief of Okaloosa County, Florida, about efforts to deliberately sink the SS United States and create an artificial reef in its wreckage.
paragraphs.zh: NPR的艾莎·拉斯科（Ayesha Rascoe）与佛罗里达州奥卡卢萨县自然资源主管亚历克斯·福格（Alex Fogg）谈论了故意将美国号客轮沉入海中并在其残骸中创建人工珊瑚礁的努力。

paragraphs.en: A historic ship docked on the Gulf Coast is getting a second life by being put down, down as in the ocean floor. This Thursday, the SS United States will be sunk on purpose to create the largest artificial reef in the world near Destin, Florida. Joining me now is Alex Fogg, the natural resources chief for Okaloosa County, Florida. Thank you so much for joining us.
paragraphs.zh: 一艘停靠在墨西哥湾沿岸的历史船正通过被下沉，也就是下沉到海底，获得第二次生命。本周四，SS美国号将被故意沉没，在佛罗里达州德斯廷附近打造世界上最大的人工珊瑚礁。现在加入我们的是佛罗里达州奥卡卢萨县的自然资源主管亚历克斯·福格。非常感谢您加入我们。

paragraphs.en: RASCOE: So first of all, tell us a little bit about the ship, its history and why it's so special.
paragraphs.zh: RASCOE：首先，请告诉我们一些关于这艘船的信息，它的历史以及为什么它如此特别。

paragraphs.en: FOGG: So the SS United States, it's huge. We've done a lot of artificial reef projects in the past, and this one really sticks out really 'cause of its size, but also its storied past. It's a vessel that was built back in the early 1950s, went back and forth to Europe. It was eventually retired in the late 1960s when air travel just became so much more efficient. But during that time, it carried all sorts of really famous people and was geared to be a troop carrier in the event of the United States getting involved in another world war.
paragraphs.zh: FOGG：所以SS United States号，非常巨大。我们过去做过很多人工礁项目，而这个项目确实非常突出，不仅因为它的规模，还因为它丰富的历史。这是一艘建造于20世纪50年代初的船，往返欧洲。到了20世纪60年代末，由于航空旅行变得更加高效，它最终退役了。但在那段时间里，它承载了各种非常有名的人物，并且设计时也考虑到如果美国卷入另一场世界大战，它可以用作运送军队的船只。

paragraphs.en: RASCOE: My understanding is that it sat for decades in Philadelphia and made its way around the world, as you talked about. But then eventually down to Florida. How did it get down to Florida?
paragraphs.zh: RASCOE: 我的理解是，它在费城搁置了数十年，然后像你说的那样走向了世界各地。但最终却到了佛罗里达。它是怎么到佛罗里达的？

paragraphs.en: FOGG: Yeah. It was a very long tow. So we had to do a lot of checks and balances with our contractor, naval architects, U.S. Coast Guard, all sorts of different entities, to make sure that it was seaworthy enough to be towed from Philadelphia all the way down to Mobile, Alabama, where the full remediation was going to occur.
paragraphs.zh: FOGG：是的。这是一次非常长的拖航。因此我们不得不与我们的承包商、海军建筑师、美国海岸警卫队以及各种不同的机构进行大量的检查和平衡，以确保它足够适航，能够从费城拖到阿拉巴马州的莫比尔，在那里将进行全面的修复。

paragraphs.en: RASCOE: Well, let's talk about the big plans for the ship's new life. Like, why would you sink a nearly 900-foot ship intentionally in the Gulf of Mexico?
paragraphs.zh: RASCOE：好吧，让我们谈谈这艘船新生活的大计划。比如，为什么你要故意把一艘接近900英尺的船沉在墨西哥湾？

paragraphs.en: FOGG: We tried to talk about or tried to figure out ways that we could increase our artificial reef construction to benefit tourism, to benefit the environment. Came up with a whole plan to acquire a bunch of vessels to sink as artificial reefs 'cause when people come diving in a destination, they don't want to dive, you know, sand, or maybe don't want to dive natural reefs all the time. They want to be a bona fide wreck diver. So by deploying these wrecks, it started to put us on the map as a dive destination, and there was a plan that if a vessel of very large size or a very cool story comes along, we would pursue it. And the SS United States was that ship.
paragraphs.zh: FOGG：我们尝试讨论或尝试找出方法来增加人工礁的建设，以惠及旅游业和环境。我们制定了一个完整的计划，打算收购一大批船只，作为人工礁沉入海底，因为当人们去某个潜水目的地潜水时，他们不想只是潜入沙子里，或者可能并不总是想潜入天然礁。他们想成为真正的沉船潜水者。所以，通过部署这些沉船，我们开始在潜水目的地地图上占有一席之地。计划是如果有一艘非常大的船或者有非常酷的故事的船出现，我们会去追求它。而美国联合号（SS United States）就是那艘船。

articles.title: Bagel makers, lovers and critics converged in New York for best bagel contest
articles.dek: The best bagel contest in New York City last weekend drew competitors from around the world, and of course lots of hometown bagel makers and critics.

paragraphs.en: The best bagel contest in New York City last weekend drew competitors from around the world, and of course lots of hometown bagel makers and critics.
paragraphs.zh: 上周末在纽约市举行的最佳贝果比赛吸引了来自世界各地的参赛者，当然还有许多本地的贝果制造者和评论家。

paragraphs.en: A beloved weekend morning ritual for many people is the bagel. Sometimes just toasted with butter or cream cheese hits the spot. Sometimes you want a full-blown bacon, egg and cheese bagel sandwich. If you are a bagel lover, you might have wished you could have attended this weekend's seventh annual BagelFest in New York. Thousands of people were there, including reporter Jeff Lunden. Here's his story.
paragraphs.zh: 许多人喜爱的周末早晨习惯之一是贝果。有时仅仅烤一下涂上黄油或奶油奶酪就足够了。有时你可能想要一份完整的培根、鸡蛋和奶酪贝果三明治。如果你是贝果爱好者，你可能会希望自己能够参加本周末在纽约举办的第七届年度贝果节。成千上万的人参加了，包括记者杰夫·伦登。这是他的报道。

paragraphs.en: JEFF LUNDEN: As a New Yorker, I appreciate a good doughy bagel. Sam Silverman, the founder of BagelFest, does too. He grew up in Massachusetts, eating bagels from Dunkin' Donuts, and loved them. But when he moved to New York...
paragraphs.zh: JEFF LUNDEN：作为一名纽约人，我很喜欢吃松软的百吉饼。BagelFest的创始人Sam Silverman也一样。他在马萨诸塞州长大，经常吃Dunkin' Donuts的百吉饼，非常喜欢它们。但当他搬到纽约时……

paragraphs.en: SAM SILVERMAN: And I had my very first bagel, real bagel from Ess-a-Bagel, it changed my life.
paragraphs.zh: SAM SILVERMAN：我吃了我的第一个百吉饼，真正的百吉饼，来自 Ess-a-Bagel，这改变了我的生活。

paragraphs.en: LUNDEN: So much so that seven years ago, he started BagelFest, and every year they crown the best in show. He says there are four criteria - flavor, texture, appearance and aroma.
paragraphs.zh: 伦登：以至于七年前，他创办了贝果节，每年他们都会评选出最佳作品。他说有四个标准——味道、质地、外观和香气。

paragraphs.en: SILVERMAN: It needs to be crunchy on the outside, soft and chewy on the inside.
paragraphs.zh: SILVERMAN：外面需要酥脆，里面要柔软有嚼劲。

paragraphs.en: SILVERMAN: From the taste perspective, we want multi notes. We want a sufficient level of salt. And then it needs to look beautiful - golden crust, nice plump shape.
paragraphs.zh: SILVERMAN：从口味的角度来看，我们希望有多层次的味道。我们希望有足够的盐分。然后它需要看起来漂亮——金色的外壳，饱满的形状。

paragraphs.en: LUNDEN: This year, there were 52 vendors, and every one of the attendees got a booklet to make notes on all the bagels so they could vote for their favorites. And the first vendor I saw was Steven Orr from Belfast. Northern Ireland.

articles.title: What to expect from Trump and Xi's upcoming meeting in China
articles.dek: Preview of what to expect as President Trump meets with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China this week.

paragraphs.en: Preview of what to expect as President Trump meets with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China this week.
paragraphs.zh: 本周，特朗普总统将在中国深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织峰会上与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京会晤，以下是此次会晤的预期情况预览。

paragraphs.en: President Trump will meet with some of the world's most powerful leaders this week. China's Xi Jinping, Russia's Vladimir Putin and President Trump will be among the attendees to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen China. But while the administration says nuclear proliferation is on the docket, all eyes will be on the U.S.-China relationship. That's now under serious strain after the scandalous departure of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, following revelations regarding a romantic relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. Evan Osnos writes for The New Yorker. He has covered China for much of his career and is closely following the APEC summit. Welcome.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普总统本周将与世界上一些最有权势的领导人会晤。中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统特朗普将出席在中国深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织峰会。但是，尽管美国政府表示核扩散问题已列入议程，但所有人的目光都将聚焦于中美关系。在曝出与一名涉嫌与中国情报部门有联系的女性存在婚外情后，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋丑闻缠身并离职，该公司的股价目前正承受着巨大压力。Evan Osnos是《纽约客》的撰稿人。他在职业生涯的大部分时间里都从事中国事务的报道，并密切关注亚太经合组织峰会。欢迎您。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: So let's start with what's been dominating headlines this week, NVIDIA. You know, this scandal is hanging over this upcoming meeting between Trump and Xi Jinping. How do you think this will set the tone?
paragraphs.zh: SCHMITZ：那么，我们先从本周占据头条新闻的英伟达说起。你知道，这桩丑闻正笼罩在即将举行的特朗普与习近平会晤之上。您认为这会如何定调？

paragraphs.en: OSNOS: Well, it is a huge development to happen right before a meeting at this altitude of two leaders. I mean, you have now a case that has brought the underlying issues right to the surface, and by that I mean the tension around technology and chips and more specifically, what the Trump administration has set out to do when it comes to allowing or restricting the export of American chips and who it's been listening to. So, you know, Jensen Huang has been one of the president's most trusted voices over the course of the last two years of this administration on technology issues. He is now gone, and so they go into this summit with a scrambled set of inputs. And it's not entirely clear how that's going to play out in the room.
paragraphs.zh: 奥斯诺斯：好吧，在两位领导人即将举行高规格会晤之际发生这样的重大事态发展。我的意思是，现在出现了一个将深层问题直接摆到台面的案例，我指的是围绕技术和芯片的紧张局势，更具体地说，就是特朗普政府在允许或限制美国芯片出口方面打算采取什么行动，以及它一直在听取谁的意见。大家都知道，在过去两年里，在本届政府处理技术问题时，Jensen Huang一直是总统最信任的声音之一。他现在已经离开了，所以他们带着一套杂乱无章的意见参加这次峰会。目前还不完全清楚这将在会场上如何展开。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: So I want to pivot to another trade issue here. This week, China extended its trade truce over rare earth exports by two more months to January 10, and for its part, the U.S. is extending tariff exclusions on 178 Chinese products until that date. What is at stake here if these two sides cannot come to an agreement?
paragraphs.zh: SCHMITZ：接下来我想转到另一个贸易问题。本周，中国将稀土出口的贸易休战期再延长两个月，至1月10日。美国方面则将178种中国产品的关税豁免期延长至该日期。如果双方无法达成协议，将面临怎样的风险？

paragraphs.en: OSNOS: Well, it's an explosive prospect. But they have managed to avoid having these full tariffs go into effect now for many months, and that's by mutual design. I mean, the - China's economy has weakness on the domestic side. They're still dealing with the outcome of a property collapse, which left 90 million houses unfilled - enough people, by the way, to house the entire population of Russia. They've had youth unemployment - at some points, up above 20%. So they were not eager to get into a trade war.
paragraphs.zh: 奥斯诺斯：嗯，这是一个爆炸性的前景。但他们设法避免了这些全额关税在过去几个月内生效，这是双方共同的意图。我的意思是，中国经济在国内方面存在弱点。他们仍在应对房地产泡沫破裂的后果，泡沫破裂导致9000万套房屋空置——顺便说一句，这些房屋足以容纳俄罗斯的全部人口。他们存在青年失业问题，在某些时候，失业率超过20%。因此，他们并不急于卷入贸易战。

paragraphs.en: And of course, on the United States' side, Donald Trump's party was just battered in the midterms partly because of the effects of tariffs introduced into trade relationships around the world. So in some ways, he's had reasons to try to hold this off. If, in fact, the truce collapses and they're not able to figure out a way to push this off, this could trigger another round of retaliatory tariffs and a spiral of retaliation that could drive up prices for American consumers. And that comes, obviously, at a moment when voters have signaled pretty loudly that they don't want to see that happen. So the stakes are high for the administration on that score.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，在美国方面，唐纳德·特朗普所在的政党刚刚在中期选举中遭遇惨败，部分原因在于对全球贸易关系征收关税所产生的影响。因此，在某种程度上，他有理由试图阻止这一局面。事实上，如果停战协议破裂，他们又无法找到办法来避免这种情况，这可能会引发新一轮的报复性关税，并导致报复行为的恶性循环，从而推高美国消费者的物价。很明显，这发生在选民大声疾呼不希望看到这种情况发生的时候。因此，在这方面，政府面临的风险很高。
