articles.title: These economists say in-person work boosts creativity, but office mandates fall short
articles.dek: A pair economists argue in a new book that people are more creative and productive when they work together in person. But it's not enough for employers to simply order workers back to the office.

paragraphs.en: A pair economists argue in a new book that people are more creative and productive when they work together in person. But it's not enough for employers to simply order workers back to the office.
paragraphs.zh: 两位经济学家在新书里指出，当人们面对面一起工作时，他们的创造力和工作效率更高。但雇主仅仅要求员工返回办公室是不够的。

paragraphs.en: Years ago, Natalia Emanuel was a graduate student at Harvard, sharing a small basement office with another budding economist, and the two wound up forming a lasting professional partnership.
paragraphs.zh: 多年前，Natalia Emanuel是哈佛大学的一名研究生，与另一位崭露头角的经济学家共用一间狭小的地下室办公室，两人最终结成了长久的专业合作伙伴关系。

paragraphs.en: NATALIA EMANUEL: We had many, many years where we were only a few feet away from each other. You could say, oh, is this a brilliant idea? Or someone could very easily say, no, that's a waste of time. Please stop.
paragraphs.zh: NATALIA EMANUEL：我们有许多许多年都只相隔几英尺。你可以说，哦，这是个好主意吗？或者有人很容易就会说，不，这纯属浪费时间。请别再说了。

paragraphs.en: SIMON: Emanuel and her one-time office mate, Emma Harrington, have now written a book on the advantages of working side by side with colleagues. It is called "In Person," and the book comes as many businesses now contend with just how in person they want their workers to be. NPR's Scott Horsley reports.
paragraphs.zh: 西蒙：埃马纽埃尔和她曾经的办公室同事艾玛·哈灵顿（Emma Harrington）现在撰写了一本书，阐述与同事并肩工作的益处。这本书名为《面对面》（In Person），正值许多企业正在权衡希望员工以何种方式面对面工作之际出版。NPR的斯科特·霍斯利（Scott Horsley）来报道。

paragraphs.en: SCOTT HORSLEY, BYLINE: The book opens with a story about Steve Jobs, who insisted that Pixar's headquarters have a central atrium where animators and engineers would naturally bump into each other. Emanuel says the man who's responsible for putting screens in all of our pockets nevertheless understood the value of connecting coworkers face to face.
paragraphs.zh: SCOTT HORSLEY，署名：这本书以一个关于史蒂夫·乔布斯的故事开篇，他坚持要求皮克斯总部设一个中央中庭，让动画师和工程师能够自然地碰面。埃马纽埃尔说，这位将屏幕装进我们所有口袋的人，却深知同事之间面对面交流的价值。

paragraphs.en: EMANUEL: You do need to have some friction, the unexpected serendipitous encounter, and those things are much, much more likely to happen in person.
paragraphs.zh: EMANUEL：你确实需要一些摩擦，一些意想不到的偶然相遇，而这些事情在面对面交流时发生的可能性要大得多。

paragraphs.en: HORSLEY: But in-person contact on the job is less common since the pandemic. Emanuel says nearly 1 out of 4 employees still works remotely, almost seven years after the outbreak began. As economists, she and Harrington have documented some of the drawbacks of that - a 20% drop in on-the-job feedback, less mentoring, which makes it harder for young people to find jobs, and more isolation, which wears on mental health. Some companies have begun to backtrack on work-from-home policies they adopted during the pandemic. In leaked audio, published by Barron's last year, JP Morgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon told employees remote work wasn't working.
paragraphs.zh: HORSLEY：但是，自疫情爆发以来，工作中的面对面接触变得不那么常见了。Emanuel表示，在疫情爆发近七年后，仍有近四分之一的员工远程办公。作为经济学家，她和哈林顿记录了其中的一些弊端——工作中的反馈减少了20%，指导也减少了，这使得年轻人更难找到工作，而且孤立感加剧，对心理健康造成了影响。一些公司已开始收回疫情期间所采用的居家办公政策。在《巴伦周刊》去年发布的泄露音频中，摩根大通首席执行官杰米·戴蒙 (Jamie Dimon) 告诉员工，远程办公行不通。

paragraphs.en: JAMIE DIMON: It slows down decision-making. The young generation is being damaged by this. They're being left behind socially, ideas, meeting people. I can't stand it anymore.
paragraphs.zh: JAMIE DIMON：它会拖慢决策过程。年轻一代正因此受到损害。他们在社交、思想、结识他人方面都落后了。我实在受不了了。

articles.title: How the tech industry and markets have responded to Jensen Huang's resignation
articles.dek: We look at the industry and market response to news that NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang was forced to step down after reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two of his employees.

paragraphs.en: We look at the industry and market response to news that NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang was forced to step down after reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two of his employees.
paragraphs.zh: 我们来关注一下行业和市场对以下消息的反应：有报道称，英伟达创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋因涉嫌与一名中国间谍以及他的两名员工有染而被逼下台。

paragraphs.en: You might have heard that Jensen Huang, founder of Nvidia and its now-former CEO, was found to have affairs with two employees as well as one with a Chinese businesswoman. The New York Times, citing U.S. intelligence, reported that the businesswoman, who was a client of Nvidia's, was recruited by China's top spy agency. China denies having anything to do with this. But the national security implications are huge, given that Nvidia designs advanced microchips and is involved in AI policy. So what now?
paragraphs.zh: 您可能听说过，英伟达的创始人兼现已卸任的首席执行官黄仁勋被曝与两名员工以及一名中国女商人有染。《纽约时报》援引美国情报部门的消息报道称，这位女商人是英伟达的客户，被中国顶级情报机构招募。中国否认与此事有任何关系。但鉴于英伟达设计先进的微芯片并参与人工智能政策的制定，其对国家安全的影响是巨大的。那么现在该怎么办呢？

paragraphs.en: Ricky Mulvey is a reporter with NPR's daily economics show, The Indicator from Planet Money. Welcome to the program.
paragraphs.zh: Ricky Mulvey是NPR每日经济节目《The Indicator from Planet Money》的记者。欢迎收听本节目。

paragraphs.en: RASCOE: Ricky, The Indicator explains a slice of the economy in 10 minutes or less. Today, you definitely have less, OK?
paragraphs.zh: RASCOE：Ricky，《经济指标》会在10分钟或更短的时间内解释经济的一个方面。今天，你绝对用不了10分钟，好吗？

paragraphs.en: RASCOE: So let's start here. Was this a failure on Nvidia's part or U.S. intelligence?
paragraphs.zh: RASCOE：那么，我们从这里开始。这是英伟达的失误还是美国情报部门的失误？

paragraphs.en: MULVEY: Yeah. So let's take the personal indiscretions out of this for a moment. Jensen Huang has a personal security team, and hopefully they know who he is closely interacting with. Jensen Huang denied knowing that she was a spy. But Alice Huang, the alleged spy, was a television presenter for Chinese state television before pivoting to tech. And when she was with Jensen, she was an executive at a computing firm called Megaspeed. And Megaspeed was allegedly bypassing U.S. export restrictions to ship advanced chips to China.
paragraphs.zh: MULVEY：是的。那么，我们暂时先不谈个人行为不检的问题。黄仁勋有一个个人安保团队，希望他们知道他与谁有密切的互动。黄仁勋否认知道她是间谍。但据称是间谍的黄静（Alice Huang）在转向科技领域之前，曾是中国中央电视台的电视节目主持人。当她与Jensen在一起时，她是名为Megaspeed的计算机公司的高管。据称，Megaspeed 绕过了美国的出口限制，向中国运送先进芯片。

paragraphs.en: Investigators at the Commerce Department raised some flags about this company a couple of years ago. They thought it was unusual that Megaspeed had Nvidia chips just packed in boxes at its data center in Malaysia - sort of like leaving Amazon packages in your entranceway, except with highly coveted AI chips.
paragraphs.zh: 几年前，商务部的调查人员就对这家公司提出了一些警示。他们认为，Megaspeed在其马来西亚数据中心将Nvidia芯片直接装在箱子里，这很不寻常——有点像把亚马逊包裹放在自家门口，只不过这些包裹里装的是炙手可热的AI芯片。

paragraphs.en: In a statement provided to NPR, Megaspeed says it conducts lawful and legitimate business and that Alice Huang left the company last year. Now, Culper Research - a short seller, or someone who bets against companies - noted their uncomfortably close relationship back in May. So in other words, there was some smoke long before this fire.
paragraphs.zh: Megaspeed在向NPR提供的一份声明中表示，该公司从事合法合规的业务，而Alice Huang已于去年离职。现在，Culper Research（一家做空机构，即做空公司股票的机构）早在5月份就注意到了他们之间令人不安的密切关系。换句话说，早在这次火灾发生之前，就已经有迹象显示出问题。

articles.title: After last year's storm, this remote Alaska town is still picking up the pieces
articles.dek: Last fall, the remnants of Typhoon Halong tore through numerous small Alaska Native villages off the road system in Western Alaska. The storm destroyed infrastructure, floated homes off their…

paragraphs.en: Last fall, the remnants of Typhoon Halong tore through numerous small Alaska Native villages off the road system in Western Alaska. The storm destroyed infrastructure, floated homes off their foundations, and displaced over a thousand people. A year later, hundreds remain displaced as the slow work of repair in a remote part of the state continues. And in one of the hardest hit communities – the small town of Kipnuk – people still aren't sure when they'll be moving back.
paragraphs.zh: 去年秋天，台风“哈隆”的残余气流席卷了阿拉斯加西部公路系统之外的众多阿拉斯加原住民小村庄。这场风暴摧毁了基础设施，将房屋从地基上掀起，导致超过1000人流离失所。一年后，由于该州偏远地区的重建工作进展缓慢，仍有数百人流离失所。而在受灾最严重的社区之一——基普努克小镇——人们仍然不确定何时能够搬回去。

paragraphs.en: The village of under 200 homes is situated on the wide open tundra and only consistently accessible by plane.
paragraphs.zh: 这个不到200户人家的村庄坐落在广阔的苔原上，只有乘坐飞机才能始终如一地抵达。

paragraphs.en: A year ago, 90% of the residences here were damaged by the remnants of Typhoon Halong, according to the State of Alaska's Emergency Operations Center. Dozens were swept off their foundations, some with families still inside. The community is now largely scattered across Alaska – some outside the region their ancestors have lived in for thousands of years.
paragraphs.zh: 据阿拉斯加州应急行动中心的数据，一年前，这里的90%的房屋都因台风“哈隆”的余威而受损。数十栋房屋被从地基上掀起，其中一些房屋里还有家人。该社区的人们现在大多分散在阿拉斯加各地，有些人甚至离开了他们祖先生活了数千年的地区。

paragraphs.en: Throughout the past year, crews have been working on repairs.
paragraphs.zh: 在过去的一年里，工作人员一直在进行维修工作。

paragraphs.en: On a clear day in August, Eddie Chuckwuk's construction crew attempted what sounded like magic: raising a building back onto its foundations using air compressors.
paragraphs.zh: 八月的一个晴朗日子，Eddie Chuckwuk的施工队尝试了一项听起来像魔法的壮举：使用空气压缩机将一栋建筑重新抬回其地基上。

paragraphs.en: Chuckwuk is one of several dozen people who have been working long days to rebuild the place where he grew up.
paragraphs.zh: Chuckwuk是数十名长期辛勤工作以重建自己成长之地的人之一。

paragraphs.en: "We're working as fast as possible as we can to get the people back in town," Chuckwuk says. "That's what I just want to see – for everybody to come back and enjoy where they grew up instead of being placed in a different place … where they're not used to. It's pretty hard."
paragraphs.zh: “我们正在尽最大努力，让人们尽快回到镇上，”Chuckwuk说。“这就是我希望看到的——每个人都能回来，在自己长大的地方安居乐业，而不是被安置在……他们不习惯的陌生地方。这真的很艰难。”

paragraphs.en: This work is critical to getting Kipnuk's homes in shape to live in again, but the town is far from being fully restored.
paragraphs.zh: 这项工作对于让基普努克的房屋恢复宜居状态至关重要，但该镇距离全面恢复还有很长的路要走。

articles.title: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy
articles.dek: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann’s legacy

paragraphs.en: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann’s legacy
paragraphs.zh: 新一代残疾人权利活动家传承朱迪·休曼的衣钵

paragraphs.en: Judy Heumann is known as the mother of the disability rights movement — yet she is lesser known than many of the other civil rights activists of her time. Now, a new film seeks to change that.
paragraphs.zh: 朱迪·休曼被誉为残疾人权利运动之母，但与她那个时代的许多其他民权活动家相比，她并不那么知名。现在，一部新电影旨在改变这一现状。

paragraphs.en: Being Heumann, the latest movie from Oscar-winning director Siân Heder, tells the story of the young woman from Brooklyn who led the movement to win the first civil rights protections in the country for people with disabilities.
paragraphs.zh: 《成为休曼》是奥斯卡获奖导演希安·海德（Siân Heder）的最新电影，讲述了一位来自布鲁克林的年轻女性的故事，她领导了一场运动，为该国残疾人争取到了首批民权保护。

paragraphs.en: Before the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) was passed in 1990, there was Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973. It was a single sentence, written into the law, promising people with disabilities the right to fair employment and access to public life without facing discrimination.
paragraphs.zh: 在1990年《美国残疾人法案》（ADA）通过之前，存在1973年《康复法案》第504条。这是一句写进法律的单句，承诺残疾人享有公平就业的权利，并有权在不受歧视的情况下参与公共生活。

paragraphs.en: But for years, there were no rules or regulations making the federal government actually enforce those protections.
paragraphs.zh: 但多年来，一直没有制定任何规则或法规来让联邦政府切实执行这些保护措施。

paragraphs.en: Until the spring of 1977, when a band of activists with disabilities decided to do something about it. Led by Heumann and Kitty Cone, activists took over the former Department of Health, Education and Welfare building in San Francisco for nearly a month — widely considered the longest sit-in of a federal building in U.S. history.
paragraphs.zh: 直到1977年春天，一群残疾人活动人士决定采取行动。在休曼和基蒂·科恩的带领下，活动人士占领了旧金山的前卫生、教育和福利部大楼近一个月，这被普遍认为是美国历史上在联邦政府大楼内举行的最长时间的静坐示威。

paragraphs.en: People across disability groups — from wheelchair users to people with intellectual and health-related disabilities — camped out, demanding, and eventually winning the passage of rules that made Section 504 enforceable. The protests paved the way for federally funded institutions like schools, libraries, city buildings and other entities to be made accessible for disabled people.
paragraphs.zh: 从轮椅使用者到智力障碍和健康相关障碍人士，各残疾人群体露营抗议，提出要求，最终促成了使第504条具有可执行性的法规通过。这些抗议活动为学校、图书馆、市政建筑和其他由联邦政府资助的机构为残疾人提供无障碍环境铺平了道路。

paragraphs.en: "Judy always said, 'disability only becomes a tragedy for me when society fails to provide the things we need to lead our lives' — job opportunities or barrier-free buildings, for example," says former NPR correspondent Joe Shapiro, who covered disability and was a friend of Heumann's until she died in 2023.
paragraphs.zh: “朱迪总是说：‘只有当社会未能提供我们过上正常生活所需的东西时，残疾才会对我来说成为一种悲剧’——例如工作机会或无障碍建筑。”前NPR记者乔·沙皮罗（Joe Shapiro）说道。他曾报道过残疾人相关新闻，并且是休曼的朋友，直到她于2023年去世。

articles.title: Fuel crisis and protests pressure Chile's far-right president
articles.dek: SANTIAGO, Chile — Chile's ultraconservative president finds himself on the back foot after just eight months in power.

paragraphs.en: SANTIAGO, Chile — Chile's ultraconservative president finds himself on the back foot after just eight months in power.
paragraphs.zh: 圣地亚哥，智利——智利的极度保守总统在执政仅八个月后就处于下风。

paragraphs.en: José Antonio Kast, a politician who spent a career railing against progressive issues, reproductive rights and welfare policies from the extreme fringes of right-wing politics, now finds himself with just 24% approval in the polls.
paragraphs.zh: 何塞·安东尼奥·卡斯特，一位政客，他的职业生涯一直在极右翼政治的边缘猛烈抨击进步议题、生育权利和福利政策，如今在民调中只有24%的支持率。

paragraphs.en: It is less than a year since Kast stormed to the presidency in December 2025 by avoiding all mention of his hardline stances on social matters, focusing instead on two hot-button issues whipped up in the national media: illegal immigration and public security.
paragraphs.zh: 自从卡斯特在2025年12月通过回避所有关于社会事务强硬立场的提及而迅速赢得总统职位，转而专注于全国媒体炒作的两个热点问题：非法移民和公共安全，已经不到一年了。

paragraphs.en: But rather than pressing ahead with those at the top of his agenda, he has floundered. And as elsewhere around the Americas and worldwide, rising costs of living have come to hit him hard.
paragraphs.zh: 但他并没有推进议程上最重要的事项，而是陷入了困境。正如美洲及世界其他地区一样，生活成本的上升对他打击甚大。

paragraphs.en: "Our salaries are maybe 20% of a European income, but with a similar cost of living – it's terrible," said Simón Echavarría, a 30-year-old architect, at a march in Santiago on Friday evening.
paragraphs.zh: 30岁的建筑师西蒙·埃查瓦里亚在星期五晚上圣地亚哥的一次游行中说：“我们的工资也许只是欧洲收入的20%，但生活成本却相似——这太糟糕了。”

paragraphs.en: "We want to protest against the measures that have set us back on environmental issues, on human rights, even reducing the sentences of pedophiles – they are implementing things that nobody asked for," he said.
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“我们想抗议那些让我们在环境问题、人权问题上倒退，甚至减轻恋童癖者刑期的措施——他们在实施没人要求的事情。”

paragraphs.en: Behind him, heavily armed police blocked the streets and fired water cannons at protesters chanting and waving flags in the square.
paragraphs.zh: 在他身后，装备精良的警察封锁了街道，并向在广场上呼喊口号、挥舞旗帜的抗议者发射了水炮。

paragraphs.en: Much of the recent ire stems from the revelation last month that Kast's government had signed decrees to cut the sentences of 56 prisoners whose crimes range from the rape of children to dictatorship-era human rights violations.
paragraphs.zh: 最近的许多愤怒源于上个月的揭露，即卡斯特政府签署法令，减轻56名囚犯的刑期，这些囚犯的犯罪行为从强奸儿童到独裁时期的人权侵犯不等。

articles.title: Commerce Department under pressure for delaying export controls on Nvidia chips
articles.dek: The U.S. Commerce Department is under scrutiny for clearing Chinese companies to handle Nvidia chips, despite national security concerns from cabinet officials and U.S. intelligence agencies.

paragraphs.en: The U.S. Commerce Department is under scrutiny for clearing Chinese companies to handle Nvidia chips, despite national security concerns from cabinet officials and U.S. intelligence agencies.
paragraphs.zh: 美国商务部因批准中国公司处理英伟达芯片而受到审查，尽管内阁官员和美国情报机构对国家安全表示担忧。

paragraphs.en: Pressure is growing on the Commerce Department and its Secretary Howard Lutnick over why Nvidia's chips have been allowed to be exported to China, despite national security concerns from cabinet officials and intelligence agencies.
paragraphs.zh: 随着内阁官员和情报机构提出国家安全方面的担忧，商务部及其部长霍华德·卢特尼克为何允许英伟达的芯片出口到中国，压力正在增加。

paragraphs.en: SCOTT BESSENT: They were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months, but commerce has the pin. Commerce BIS has the pin, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes.
paragraphs.zh: SCOTT BESSENT：他们几个月来一直支持将Megaspeed列入实体清单，但商务部掌握着关键权力。商务部BIS掌握着关键权力，你需要向他们询问其内部流程。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: That is Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accusing Lutnick's department of not putting Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm with suspected Chinese intelligence ties, on the federal trade restriction list. Liza Tobin is former China director for the National Security Council in the first Trump and Biden administrations. She's here with us now to discuss this. Welcome.
paragraphs.zh: 施密茨：这是财政部长斯科特·贝森特指责卢特尼克的部门没有将Megaspeed（一家总部位于新加坡、与中国情报有嫌疑联系的公司）列入联邦贸易限制名单。莉萨·托宾曾在特朗普和拜登的第一届政府中担任国家安全委员会的中国事务主任。她现在和我们在一起讨论此事。欢迎她。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: So you're watching this situation unfold very closely. Tell me your reaction to these accusations against Secretary Lutnick.
paragraphs.zh: 施密茨：所以你正在密切关注这一情况的发展。告诉我你对这些针对卢特尼克国务卿的指控有何反应。

paragraphs.en: TOBIN: Commerce has the pen. Commerce is the agency that has been given the statutory authority by the Congress to regulate the export of these AI chips. They're the ones that write the rules. They also have a law enforcement role. Right now, the whole cover has been blown off this scandal, and Lutnick is there at the center, and it's clear that he just didn't do his job in enforcing those rules.
paragraphs.zh: 托宾：商务部掌握着笔杆子。商务部是国会赋予法定权力来监管这些人工智能芯片出口的机构。他们才是制定规则的人。他们也承担执法职责。现在，这场丑闻的整个内幕已经被揭露出来，而卢特尼克正处在风口浪尖，很明显他在执行这些规则时根本没有尽到自己的职责。

paragraphs.en: TOBIN: So that is the trillion-dollar question. I think we're going to find out a lot more as Congress starts to dig into this. I think we're going to learn a lot more about, was Howard Lutnick benefiting from this regulatory capture? You know, he...
paragraphs.zh: 托宾：所以这就是那个万亿问题。我认为随着国会开始深入调查这一点，我们将会发现更多。我认为我们会更多地了解，霍华德·卢特尼克是否从这种监管俘获中受益？你知道，他……

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: Well, I mean, we do know that Cantor Fitzgerald, a firm run by Lutnick's sons Brandon and Kyle, helps place companies that run data centers in Asia, and their firm has a financial interest in looser chip restrictions that Lutnick himself was in charge of implementing. That seems like a conflict of interest, no?
paragraphs.zh: SCHMITZ：嗯，我是说，我们确实知道 Cantor Fitzgerald，这是一家由卢特尼克的儿子布兰登和凯尔经营的公司，帮助将经营数据中心的公司引入亚洲，而且他们的公司在卢特尼克自己负责实施的更宽松芯片限制中有经济利益。这看起来像是利益冲突，不是吗？

articles.title: Hello? James Gleick's new book compares the history of the telephone to the modern era
articles.dek: Have you ever wondered where phone etiquette or the idea for the first social network came from? Author James Gleick talks about his new book, The Telephone.

paragraphs.en: Have you ever wondered where phone etiquette or the idea for the first social network came from? Author James Gleick talks about his new book, The Telephone.
paragraphs.zh: 你是否曾想过电话礼仪或第一个社交网络的概念是从哪里来的？作者詹姆斯·格雷克谈论了他的新书《电话》。

paragraphs.en: You know, this is the first time I've noticed this, but here in the cafeteria, in the corner, there is a telephone booth, and I'm going to get into this booth right now, and I'm going to call our next guest.
paragraphs.zh: 你知道，这是我第一次注意到这个，但在这里的自助餐厅的角落里，有一个电话亭，我现在要进去这个电话亭，我要给我们的下一位嘉宾打电话。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: Hello, this is Rob Schmitz at NPR. We're talking to you about a book you wrote. It's called "The Telephone: A New History." Welcome.
paragraphs.zh: 施密茨：你好，我是NPR的罗布·施密茨。我们正在和你谈论你写的一本书。它叫《电话：新历史》。欢迎。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: So, James, there's a good chunk of your book all about the development of the etiquette of answering the phone. So how did I do there?
paragraphs.zh: 施密茨：所以，詹姆斯，你的书里有相当一部分内容是关于接电话礼仪的发展。那么我那方面做得怎么样？

paragraphs.en: GLEICK: I mean, the fact that we say hello - and it's not just English speakers. It's - people in many countries say hello or some version of allo (ph).
paragraphs.zh: GLEICK：我的意思是，我们说‘你好’这一事实——而且不仅仅是讲英语的人。很多国家的人都会说‘你好’或某种形式的‘allo’。

paragraphs.en: GLEICK: What's weird is that's a telephone word. That word was not in particularly common use before the telephone arrived. And when Alexander Graham Bell and his assistant Tom Watson started making their first phone calls along an open line, you know, they used to say, ahoy, ahoy.
paragraphs.zh: GLEICK：奇怪的是，那是一个电话用语。在电话出现之前，这个词并不是特别常用。当亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔和他的助手汤姆·沃森沿着一条开放线路开始拨打他们的第一个电话时，你知道，他们过去常说，‘喂，喂’。

paragraphs.en: GLEICK: But within a couple of years, just as if God had sent a memo, everybody was using the word hello.
paragraphs.zh: 格雷克：但是仅仅几年之后，就好像上帝发了一份备忘录一样，每个人都在使用‘你好’这个词。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: When I grew up in the 1970s and '80s, I was sometimes told by my parents to answer the phone, Schmitz residence, Robert speaking.
paragraphs.zh: 施密茨：当我在1970年代和1980年代长大时，父母有时会告诉我接电话时说，施密茨家，罗伯特在说话。

articles.title: Oyster stocks have plunged in the Chesapeake. This resident wants to bring them back
articles.dek: John Consoli stands on the edge of his pier, which juts out from the southern tip of Maryland's Kent Island and into the Chesapeake Bay. He leans over and hoists a mesh the size and shape of a…

paragraphs.en: John Consoli stands on the edge of his pier, which juts out from the southern tip of Maryland's Kent Island and into the Chesapeake Bay. He leans over and hoists a mesh the size and shape of a pillowcase out of the water.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰·康索利站在他的码头边缘，码头从马里兰州肯特岛南端伸出，延伸到切萨皮克湾。他弯下腰，把一个大小和枕套一样的网从水中提了上来。

paragraphs.en: It's packed with oysters. He manages to get it onto the pier. "These are brand new oysters from this year," he says. "When I got them, they weighed nothing. And this is just three months of growth. The net is chock full, I can hardly pull it up."
paragraphs.zh: 里面满是牡蛎。他设法把它弄到码头上。“这些是今年的新牡蛎，”他说。“当我拿到它们时，几乎没重量。这只是三个月的生长。网满得不得了，我几乎拉不上来。”

paragraphs.en: Once he catches his breath, Consoli marvels at these molluscs. "I think I'm more enthusiastic about something that's like a rock than anybody else could possibly be," he says with a big grin. "I really can't think of many more creatures that do the good that oysters do."
paragraphs.zh: 一旦他喘过气来，康索利便惊叹于这些软体动物。“我想我对像岩石一样的东西可能比任何人都更热情，”他带着大大的笑容说。“我真的想不出还有多少生物能像牡蛎那样做好事。”

paragraphs.en: Oysters underpin the Chesapeake's coastal and estuarine ecosystem. Each adult filters up to 50 gallons of water a day. Cleaner water leads to a healthier bay and more sea grass. "That helps crabs and other organisms," says Consoli.
paragraphs.zh: 牡蛎支撑着切萨皮克湾的沿海和河口生态系统。每只成年牡蛎每天可以过滤多达50加仑的水。水质更清洁意味着海湾更健康，海草更多。“这对螃蟹和其他生物都有帮助，”康索利说。

paragraphs.en: Plus, oyster shells are a habitat unto themselves. "Because of all the nooks and crannies," he explains, "a lot of small fish and crabs live and eat amongst them and hide, so it creates a biodiverse environment. I even found a seahorse, which was incredible. I've never seen a seahorse in my life!"
paragraphs.zh: 此外，牡蛎壳本身就是一个栖息地。他解释说：“因为有这么多的角落和缝隙，许多小鱼和螃蟹在其中生活、觅食和藏身，因此它创造了一个生物多样化的环境。我甚至发现了一只海马，这太不可思议了。我这辈子从未见过海马！”

paragraphs.en: Oyster reefs used to abound in the Chesapeake, but overharvesting decimated their ranks — by over 99% by 2011, according to one estimate. This monumental shift in the bay contributed to poorer water quality and less habitat for other species.
paragraphs.zh: 牡蛎礁曾经在切萨皮克湾大量存在，但过度捕捞摧毁了它们的数量——据一项估计，到2011年减少了超过99%。这一巨大变化导致海湾水质下降，并为其他物种留下的栖息地减少。

paragraphs.en: Oyster farming in the Chesapeake has expanded in recent years, despite environmental and disease challenges, says Ryan Carnegie, a biologist at the Virginia Institute of Marine Science. He adds that wild oysters have also made a partial comeback, helped by better management and investments in restoration. But, says Elizabeth North, a fisheries oceanographer at the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science, "there is still a lot of room to grow."
paragraphs.zh: 弗吉尼亚海洋科学研究所的生物学家瑞安·卡内基表示，尽管面临环境和疾病的挑战，切萨皮克湾的牡蛎养殖近年来仍在扩大。他补充说，野生牡蛎也有所部分恢复，这得益于更好的管理和恢复投资。但马里兰大学环境科学中心的渔业海洋学家伊丽莎白·诺斯表示，“仍有很大的增长空间。”

paragraphs.en: Consoli's goal, therefore, is to be a caretaker of sorts, stocking the bay with ever more oysters and looking after their wellbeing. He floats them just below the surface where he says the nutrients are concentrated to help them grow quickly. And although his oysters aren't intended for eating, a cleaner bay does mean better habitat for those that are harvested commercially.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，Consoli 的目标是成为某种照管者，为海湾储存越来越多的牡蛎并照顾它们的健康。他将牡蛎漂浮在水面下方，他说那里营养物质集中，有助于它们快速生长。尽管他的牡蛎并不用于食用，但清洁的海湾确实意味着为商业采收的牡蛎提供了更好的栖息环境。

articles.title: M. John Harrison makes history as first sci-fi author to win the Booker Prize
articles.dek: M. John Harrison has become the first science fiction author to win the prestigious Booker Prize, for "The End of Everything," in a milestone for the genre.

paragraphs.en: M. John Harrison has become the first science fiction author to win the prestigious Booker Prize, for "The End of Everything," in a milestone for the genre.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰·哈里森先生成为首位获得享有盛誉的布克奖的科幻小说作家，他凭借《万物终结》获得此奖，这对于该类型是一个里程碑。

paragraphs.en: Every year, the Booker Prize honors the best fiction published in the U.K. and Ireland. It is one of the highest achievements in English-language literature. Past winners include Salman Rushdie for "Midnight's Children," Hilary Mantel for "Wolf Hall" and Kazuo Ishiguro for "The Remains Of The Day." This year, the prize went to M. John Harrison's "The End Of Everything," and it is the first science fiction novel to win the Booker in the prize's nearly six-decade history. What took so long? What's it mean for the genre? NPR's Andrew Limbong is here. Andrew, thanks so much for being with us.
paragraphs.zh: 每年，布克奖都会表彰在英国和爱尔兰出版的最佳小说。它是英语文学中最高的成就之一。过去的获奖者包括萨尔曼·鲁西迪的《午夜之子》、希拉里·曼特尔的《狼厅》和石黑一雄的《剩物之日》。今年，该奖颁给了M. 约翰·哈里森的《万物终结》，这是该奖近六十年历史上首部获奖的科幻小说。为什么会花这么长时间？这对这个类型意味着什么？NPR的安德鲁·林邦在这里。安德鲁，非常感谢你加入我们。

paragraphs.en: SIMON: I'm embarrassed to say I hadn't heard of the book. Tell us about it.
paragraphs.zh: 西蒙：我不好意思地说我没听说过这本书。给我们介绍一下吧。

paragraphs.en: LIMBONG: So it's set in this dystopian near future, but it's not exactly clear at the start what's happened that's caused this dystopian future. And we begin by following this guy named Phillip, who's a beachcomber. So he spends his time along the southern coast of England looking for stuff to sell. And he comes across this blob. It's hard to explain, but it's this shape-shifting thing that grows and regenerates. It ends up talking, and Phillip takes it under his care. All the while in the background, we're being given this information about an alien invasion, the iGhetti. But again, it is not super-duper clear what kind of aliens these are or what, really, the invasion itself caused.
paragraphs.zh: LIMBONG：所以故事设定在一个反乌托邦的近未来，但一开始并不完全清楚导致这个反乌托邦未来发生了什么。我们一开始跟随一个名叫菲利普的人，他是个拾荒者。他在英格兰南海岸沿岸寻找可以出售的东西。有一天，他遇到了一个无法轻易描述的东西，是一种会改变形状、不断生长和再生的生物。它最终会说话，菲利普开始照顾它。与此同时，背景中我们会被提供一些关于外星人入侵的消息，即iGhetti。但同样地，这些外星人到底是什么样的，入侵本身又真正造成了什么，并不是非常清楚。

paragraphs.en: SIMON: And I gather M. John Harrison isn't one of those novelists who overexplain circumstances...
paragraphs.zh: 西蒙：我听说约翰·哈里森先生并不是那种会过度解释情节的小说家……

paragraphs.en: LIMBONG: (Laughter) No. No, no, absolutely not. This is very much a vibes-based book. And it's a pretty slim one, too. This is, like, under 200 pages.
paragraphs.zh: LIMBONG：（笑）不。不，不，绝对不。这本书非常依赖氛围。而且它相当薄，大约不到200页。

paragraphs.en: LIMBONG: It's been bananas, Scott. It's been bonkers. This is a bit of a divisive book, and I think intentionally so. When M. John Harrison accepted the award, he started by saying he didn't think he'd end up winning. And I don't think that's false modesty. I'm inclined to believe him, judging by the reaction. The book has under three stars out of five on Goodreads, same on StoryGraph. He beat out authors sort of beloved by litfic (ph) fans and critics. You know, you got Marlon James, Elizabeth Strout, Douglas Stuart, which means, you know, there are a lot of people who are displeased by this win, to say the least.
paragraphs.zh: LIMBONG：真是疯狂，Scott。真是狂热。这本书有点分裂人群，我觉得这是故意的。当M. John Harrison接受奖项时，他开始时说他没想到自己会获奖。我认为这并非是假谦虚。从反应来看，我倾向于相信他。这本书在Goodreads上评分不到五颗星中的三颗，StoryGraph上也是如此。他战胜了一些受文学小说粉丝和评论家喜爱的作者。你知道，有Marlon James、Elizabeth Strout、Douglas Stuart，这意味着，至少可以说，有很多人对这个获奖结果不满意。

paragraphs.en: SIMON: There have been, over the past 50 years, a lot of great science fiction novels. What do you think put this one over the top?
paragraphs.zh: 西蒙：在过去的50年里，有许多伟大的科幻小说。你认为是什么让这本书脱颖而出？

articles.title: What's Trump's strategy now with Iran? To keep things as they are
articles.dek: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — President Trump is confronting new realities nine months into the war with Iran that leave him with dwindling options to ending the conflict.

paragraphs.en: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — President Trump is confronting new realities nine months into the war with Iran that leave him with dwindling options to ending the conflict.
paragraphs.zh: 阿拉伯联合酋长国迪拜——与伊朗的战争已持续九个月，特朗普总统正面临新的现实，他结束这场冲突的选项越来越少。

paragraphs.en: On Thursday, he waved away the need for a deal with Iran, saying the U.S. has billions of Iran's dollars frozen in overseas accounts.
paragraphs.zh: 周四，他否认了与伊朗达成协议的必要性，并表示美国在海外账户中冻结了伊朗数十亿美元的资金。

paragraphs.en: "We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We've got their money," he wrote in a Truth Social post.
paragraphs.zh: “我们不需要与伊朗达成协议。那些日子早已一去不复返了。我们拿到了他们的钱。”他在Truth Social上发帖写道。

paragraphs.en: Negotiations with Iran are stuck with mediator Qatar working to bridge the divide. Trump met Qatar's prime minister at the White House this week, and said afterward that Gulf Arab allies prefer "the status quo" of continued economic pressure on Iran. He wrote that while the U.S. remains "locked and loaded," an attack at this point "seems to be quite unlikely."
paragraphs.zh: 与伊朗的谈判陷入僵局，调解国卡塔尔正努力弥合分歧。本周，特朗普在白宫会见了卡塔尔首相，会后表示，海湾阿拉伯盟友更倾向于继续对伊朗施加经济压力的“现状”。他写道，虽然美国仍然“严阵以待”，但目前看来“发动袭击的可能性相当小”。

paragraphs.en: That's a pivot from his threats to carry out quick, intense strikes on Iran in the days before he had to contend with two election setbacks.
paragraphs.zh: 这是他从威胁要在其不得不应对两次选举挫折的前几天对伊朗发动快速、猛烈打击的立场上发生的转变。

paragraphs.en: Trump's wartime ally, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whom he'd thrown his support behind, is on the cusp of being ousted from power after elections there.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普在战争时期的盟友、以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡（Benjamin Netanyahu）得到了他的支持，但在以色列大选后即将被赶下台。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, at home, Trump's party lost its majority in Congress in midterm elections. Vice President Vance blamed Republican losses on the unpopular war with Iran and the nature of U.S. relations with Israel.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，在国内，特朗普的政党在中期选举中失去了国会多数席位。万斯副总统将共和党的失利归咎于不受欢迎的对伊战争以及美国与以色列关系的性质。

paragraphs.en: With less room to room maneuver and Iran still defiant, Trump's strategy appears to be to keep things as they are, for now. That means the possibility of escalation still looms.
paragraphs.zh: 由于回旋余地较小，且伊朗仍态度强硬，特朗普的策略似乎是暂时维持现状。这意味着局势升级的可能性仍然存在。

articles.title: Is there an opening for Nvidia's competitors, now that Jensen Huang is out?
articles.dek: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with Dylan Patel of the AI and semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis about Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and whether it opens up the field for Nvidia's competitors.

paragraphs.en: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with Dylan Patel of the AI and semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis about Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and whether it opens up the field for Nvidia's competitors.
paragraphs.zh: NPR的Scott Detrow与人工智能和半导体研究公司SemiAnalysis的Dylan Patel讨论了Jensen Huang离开英伟达一事，以及这是否为英伟达的竞争对手打开了局面。

paragraphs.en: Nvidia has long been the kingpin of the semiconductor industry, a company whose huge technological bets paid off, making its chips the most in-demand chips in the world and crowning the company, for a time, the most valuable in the world. But with Nvidia's leader, Jensen Huang, out, does that leave an opening for Nvidia's competitors to catch up? We're going to put that question to Dylan Patel. He is founder and CEO of SemiAnalysis, an AI and semiconductor research firm. Welcome to ALL THINGS CONSIDERED.
paragraphs.zh: 英伟达长期以来一直是半导体行业的龙头老大，该公司的大胆技术押注获得了回报，使其芯片成为全球最受欢迎的芯片，并一度使该公司成为全球市值最高的公司。但是，随着英伟达的掌门人黄仁勋的离场，这是否为英伟达的竞争对手提供了赶超的机会？我们将向Dylan Patel提出这个问题。他是人工智能和半导体研究公司SemiAnalysis的创始人兼首席执行官。欢迎收听《ALL THINGS CONSIDERED》。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: So you and others have estimated Nvidia is probably a year, two years ahead of its competitors. With Huang out, can other companies catch up?
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：所以，您和其他人估计，英伟达可能比竞争对手领先一两年。黄仁勋离任后，其他公司能赶上吗？

paragraphs.en: PATEL: I think that's the biggest risk at least. Over the last, you know, handful of years, Nvidia's lead has actually lessened, and so therefore, they've lost market share, albeit, the market has grown so fast, Nvidia's revenue and profits have skyrocketed so fast. But now, with, you know, many barbarians at the gate, when sort of Jensen is needed most, he sort of is disappearing or (inaudible) the game.
paragraphs.zh: PATEL：我认为这至少是最大的风险。在过去的几年里，Nvidia的领先优势实际上有所缩小，因此，他们失去了市场份额，尽管市场增长非常快，Nvidia的收入和利润也飙升得非常快。但现在，你知道的，门外有许多野蛮人，在最需要Jensen的时候，他似乎在消失或（听不清）这场游戏。

paragraphs.en: PATEL: I think most - the most to the company. The industry has for a long time tried to roll their own solution, you know, at least as far as the biggest customers. Google, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon all have been working on their own AI chips for, you know, a number of years. And yet, they all still relied on Nvidia. But their reliance is reducing to some extent, and that's their goal and has been their goal. And now, you know, the only way Nvidia can keep their market share and stay on top of the world is if they out execute everyone - right? - they keep innovating and bringing new technology to the market. But without Jensen, you know, the founder and the visionary of the company, it's going to be a lot harder for them to keep on top.
paragraphs.zh: PATEL：我认为对公司来说影响最大。长期以来，业界一直在尝试推出自己的解决方案，至少就最大的客户而言是这样。谷歌、微软、Meta、亚马逊都在开发自己的AI芯片，已经有好几年了。然而，他们仍然都依赖英伟达。但他们的依赖程度正在一定程度上降低，这就是他们的目标，也一直是他们的目标。现在，你知道，Nvidia能够保持其市场份额并稳居世界巅峰的唯一途径就是超越所有竞争对手——对吧？他们不断创新，并将新技术推向市场。但如果没有Jensen——公司的创始人兼有远见的领导者——他们将很难继续保持领先地位。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: One of the things you've written about that I think is really important to understand is the way that - like, sometimes I feel like a CEO's role in a company is overblown. But how much came to (ph) his personal decisions, his personal decision-making? Let's talk about this first on the supply side. How was his personal relationships with supply chain managers in Korea and Taiwan so key to Nvidia getting what it needed?
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：您写过的一些内容中，我认为非常需要理解的一点是——比如，有时我觉得CEO在公司中的作用被夸大了。但是，他的个人决定、他的个人决策起到了多大作用？我们先从供应端谈起。他与韩国和台湾供应链经理的个人关系为何对英伟达获得所需资源如此关键？

paragraphs.en: PATEL: There's no other company in the supply chain, including in the semiconductor supply chain, where the CEO is, every quarter, meeting with all his suppliers. And, you know, chips are such a complex supply chain. He has hundreds of suppliers. He's talking to every single one of them, going to Korea, going to Taiwan, going to China, meeting, having drinks with them, going to local fried chicken spots, or, you know, night food markets, everything to woo them. And given this is such a complex industry where, you know, products are improving by 2x a year - right? - it's at an incredible pace - you need your suppliers to have full focus and put their best engineers on your product. And this just keeps Nvidia ahead of everyone.
paragraphs.zh: PATEL：在供应链中，包括半导体供应链中，没有哪家公司的首席执行官会每个季度都与所有供应商会面。你知道的，芯片的供应链非常复杂。他有数百家供应商。他与他们中的每一个人都进行了交谈，去了韩国、台湾、中国，与他们见面、一起喝酒，去当地的炸鸡店，或者，你知道的，去夜市，总之就是想尽一切办法来吸引他们。而且，考虑到这是一个非常复杂的行业，产品每年都在以两倍的速度改进——对吧？——速度快得令人难以置信——你需要供应商全力以赴，派出他们最优秀的工程师来负责你的产品。这让英伟达一直遥遥领先。

articles.title: Microsoft outage disrupts work and gives some a chance to unplug
articles.dek: Millions of individuals, organizations and businesses were left without access to Microsoft's Outlook email on Thursday. Some people celebrated a day without email, while others work around obstacles.

paragraphs.en: Millions of individuals, organizations and businesses were left without access to Microsoft's Outlook email on Thursday. Some people celebrated a day without email, while others work around obstacles.
paragraphs.zh: 周四，数百万个人、组织和企业无法访问微软的Outlook电子邮件。有些人欢庆没有电子邮件的一天，而其他人则想方设法克服障碍。

paragraphs.en: Microsoft says it is seeing broad recovery and stability following a massive outage of its Outlook email system and other applications yesterday. The company says it was a technical issue not related to AI agents. The outage hit millions of Microsoft users in more than 70 countries. NPR workplace correspondent Andrea Hsu hit the phones to find out how people weathered the disruption.
paragraphs.zh: 微软表示，在昨天其Outlook电子邮件系统和其他应用程序发生大规模宕机之后，目前正在全面恢复并趋于稳定。该公司表示，这是一个与AI代理无关的技术问题。这次服务中断影响了70多个国家/地区的数百万微软用户。NPR工作场所记者Andrea Hsu拨打电话，了解人们是如何应对这次服务中断的。

paragraphs.en: ANDREA HSU, BYLINE: As president of the Global Healthy Living Foundation, Seth Ginsberg spends long days communicating with patients, doctors and government officials in the U.S., as well as Canada, Australia and Japan.
paragraphs.zh: ANDREA HSU，署名：作为全球健康生活基金会（Global Healthy Living Foundation）的总裁，Seth Ginsberg每天花很长时间与美国、加拿大、澳大利亚和日本的患者、医生和政府官员沟通。

paragraphs.en: HSU: Some 200 emails a day. But starting midday yesterday, for 20 hours, he heard nothing. For someone who's dedicated his career to improving the quality of life for people with chronic illnesses, it was jarring.
paragraphs.zh: HSU：每天大约200封电子邮件。但从昨天中午开始，整整20个小时，他都没有收到任何消息。对于一个毕生致力于改善慢性病患者生活质量的人来说，这令人不安。

paragraphs.en: GINSBERG: It was almost like an existential crisis because I went from feeling incredibly productive to wondering whether anyone needed me anymore.
paragraphs.zh: GINSBERG：这几乎像是一场存在主义危机，因为我从感觉自己富有创造力，变成了怀疑是否还有人需要我。

paragraphs.en: HSU: Once his tech team assured him that his emails would come through eventually, he settled in with pad and paper, worked on some follow-up notes from a rheumatology conference last week.
paragraphs.zh: HSU：在技术团队向他保证电子邮件最终会送达后，他坐下来，拿起记事本和纸笔，开始整理上周风湿病学会议的一些后续笔记。

paragraphs.en: GINSBERG: The funny part is how we're all so conditioned to respond to email that when it stops, we assume something terrible has happened. And apparently now, like, peace and quiet is a technical malfunction.
paragraphs.zh: GINSBERG：有趣的是，我们都习惯于回复电子邮件，以至于当电子邮件停止时，我们会以为发生了什么可怕的事情。现在看来，宁静祥和似乎是一种技术故障。

paragraphs.en: HSU: Now, even without email, people couldn't stay away from their devices. Social media was flooded with posts. On TikTok, Reba McEntire shared a song as she wondered why her inbox was quiet.
paragraphs.zh: HSU：现在，即使没有电子邮件，人们也离不开自己的设备。社交媒体上充斥着各种帖子。在TikTok上，Reba McEntire分享了一首歌，同时她也想知道为什么她的收件箱里没有新邮件。

articles.title: Plans for a data center threaten scenic wilderness and dark skies in West Virginia
articles.dek: DAVIS, W.Va. — Stretching nearly a million acres through the rugged mountains of eastern West Virginia, the Monongahela National Forest links some of the state's best known natural attractions.…

paragraphs.en: DAVIS, W.Va. — Stretching nearly a million acres through the rugged mountains of eastern West Virginia, the Monongahela National Forest links some of the state's best known natural attractions. The vast area ranges from the ski slopes of Canaan Valley to the dark skies of Blackwater Falls and Spruce Knob and includes the small towns of Davis and Thomas that serve as gateways for visitors to the region.
paragraphs.zh: 西弗吉尼亚州戴维斯——莫农加希拉国家森林绵延近100万英亩，横亘于西弗吉尼亚州东部的崎岖山脉之间，将该州一些最著名的自然景点串联起来。这片广阔的区域从迦南谷的滑雪坡道一直延伸到黑水瀑布和云杉秃顶的黑暗天空，并包括戴维斯和托马斯这两个小镇，它们是游客进入该地区的门户。

paragraphs.en: For the past seven months, Kaleb Skelton, his wife, Ella, their 2-year-old son, Ryder, and dog Mabel have lived in a camper in this corner of West Virginia's "almost heaven." Kaleb is finishing a seasonal stint as a campground manager on a lake near Spruce Knob, the state's highest point.
paragraphs.zh: 在过去的七个月里，Kaleb Skelton、他的妻子Ella、他们2岁的儿子Ryder以及狗狗Mabel一直住在西弗吉尼亚州“近乎天堂”一隅的一辆露营车里。Kaleb即将结束在斯普鲁斯诺布（该州最高点）附近一个湖畔露营地担任季节性经理的工作。

paragraphs.en: On clear nights atop the isolated peak, they get to experience a river of stars in one of the very few pockets of darkness remaining in the Eastern United States. The area has become a draw for amateur astronomers.
paragraphs.zh: 在晴朗的夜晚，他们站在这座与世隔绝的山巅上，可以欣赏到星河灿烂，这里是美国东部为数不多的几处黑暗之地之一。该地区已成为吸引业余天文学家的胜地。

paragraphs.en: During summer's new moons, Kaleb says, one in four campsites he oversees is occupied by someone with a telescope. He thought his family's cabin in eastern Texas offered "the craziest" dark skies he'd ever seen, "but coming out here definitely rivals it."
paragraphs.zh: Kaleb说，在夏季的新月期间，他负责的营地中每四处就有一处被带着望远镜的人占据。他认为，他家位于德克萨斯州东部的小木屋能看到他有生以来「最令人惊叹」的夜空，「但来到这里，这里的夜空绝对不遑多让。」

paragraphs.en: Those inky-black nights — and the natural beauty they shelter — are now under threat from what many residents see as a modern-day version of extractive industries like logging and mining that once defined the region. In a place where tourism, outdoor recreation and community are deeply intertwined, a gigantic power plant and data center campus in nearby Tucker County would bring large-scale development into the heart of it all.
paragraphs.zh: 那些漆黑的夜晚，以及它们所庇护的自然美景，如今正受到许多居民眼中现代版采掘业的威胁，这些采掘业包括伐木和采矿，它们曾是该地区的标志性产业。在一个旅游业、户外休闲和社区紧密交织的地方，位于附近塔克县的一座庞大的发电厂和数据中心园区将把大规模开发带入这一切的核心。

paragraphs.en: A stark image of the town of Davis from 1885, during the heyday of logging, is a reminder of that transformation. The photo shows a handful of squat buildings amid a broad clearing littered with forest remains.
paragraphs.zh: 一张摄于 1885 年（伐木业鼎盛时期）的戴维斯镇照片生动地再现了那段变革历史。照片中，几栋矮矮的建筑坐落在宽阔的空地上，四周散落着森林的残骸。

paragraphs.en: They used to call it "Stump Town," says Kim Williams, president of the Snow Sports Museum of West Virginia in Canaan Valley. At the turn of the century, massive first-growth trees dominated the landscape.
paragraphs.zh: 西弗吉尼亚州卡南谷雪上运动博物馆馆长金·威廉斯（Kim Williams）说：“他们以前管这里叫‘树桩镇’。” 在世纪之交，高大的原生林树木主宰着这片景观。

paragraphs.en: Then, logging companies "came in and clear-cut the whole valley and everything around it," he says.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，伐木公司“进驻并砍伐了整个山谷及其周围的一切”，他说。

articles.title: In different ways, these 2 new films take on the craft and the business of filmmaking
articles.dek: Pedro Almodovar's Bitter Christmas and Peter Farrelly's I Play Rocky are dramas that depict filmmakers creating films. Though different in style, they have much in common.

paragraphs.en: Pedro Almodovar's Bitter Christmas and Peter Farrelly's I Play Rocky are dramas that depict filmmakers creating films. Though different in style, they have much in common.
paragraphs.zh: 佩德罗·阿莫多瓦的《苦涩的圣诞节》和彼得·法拉利的《我扮演洛奇》都是描写电影人创作电影的剧情片。虽然风格不同，但它们有很多共同之处。

paragraphs.en: Write what you know is probably the most time-honored advice you can give a storyteller. Maybe these days, it should be film what you know.
paragraphs.zh: “写你所知道的”可能是你能给一个讲故事的人最经久不衰的建议。也许在如今这个时代，它应该变成“拍摄你所知道的”。

paragraphs.en: UNIDENTIFIED ACTOR: (As character) Cut. All right, we're moving in.
paragraphs.zh: 身份不明的演员：（扮演角色）停。好了，我们要进去了。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: Critic Bob Mondello says that's what moviemakers are doing in two new films about filmmaking, "Bitter Christmas" and "I Play Rocky."
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：影评人鲍勃·蒙德洛（Bob Mondello）说，这就是电影制片人在两部关于电影制作的新片《苦涩的圣诞节》（Bitter Christmas）和《我演洛奇》（I Play Rocky）中所做的事情。

paragraphs.en: BOB MONDELLO, BYLINE: At the beginning of "Bitter Christmas," we hear the sound of typing on a keyboard as the words - a film by Almodóvar - appear on the screen, and that clickety-click keeps returning because the folks we're watching, a filmmaker named Elsa and her firefighter boyfriend Bo, are fictional characters in a movie that's being written by Raúl, a real filmmaker. Well, real being relative, of course, since Raúl is himself a fictional character created by Almodóvar. The plot turns on how moviemakers inevitably use what they see around them and maybe shouldn't. The fictional Elsa, for instance, models her new script on the failing marriage of a friend, which of course, infuriates the friend.
paragraphs.zh: BOB MONDELLO，署名：在《苦涩的圣诞节》开头，我们听到键盘打字的声音，同时屏幕上出现“阿莫多瓦执导的电影”的字样。这种哒哒哒的声音不断响起，因为我们正在观看的人物——名叫埃尔莎的电影人和她的消防员男友博——是虚构角色，出现在一部由真正的电影人劳尔正在撰写的电影中。当然，真实性是相对的，因为劳尔本身就是阿尔莫多瓦虚构的人物。剧情围绕着电影人不可避免地使用他们周围所见的事物，而这些事物也许不应该被使用。例如，虚构的艾尔莎以朋友失败的婚姻为蓝本创作她的新剧本，这当然激怒了这位朋友。

paragraphs.en: MONDELLO: And since Elsa is herself modeled on Raúl's assistant, Mónica, Mónica's just as ticked off at Raúl.
paragraphs.zh: MONDELLO：既然Elsa本身是以Raúl的助理Mónica为原型，那么Mónica对Raúl的怨气也同样大。

paragraphs.en: MONDELLO: Happily, all this introspection is augmented by campy melodrama. Elsa's fictional boyfriend isn't just a firefighter. He moonlights as a stripper. And Raúl's assistant Mónica gets to critique not just the film within a film that's ticked her off, but all of Raúl's career and, by extension, Almodóvar's. Though, of course, since he's calling the shots, that means Almodóvar is doing the critiquing. The effect would be dizzying even without the black sand beaches and blazing scarlet and gold wardrobe, visual notes that keep "Bitter Christmas" firmly in the Almodóvar canon.
paragraphs.zh: MONDELLO：幸运的是，所有这些自我反思都因夸张的戏剧性情节而得到增强。埃尔莎的虚构男友不仅仅是一名消防员。他还兼职当脱衣舞男。而劳尔的助理莫妮卡不仅要批评让她恼火的片中片，还要批评劳尔的整个职业生涯，进而批评阿尔莫多瓦。当然，既然他是说了算的，那就意味着是阿尔莫多瓦在进行批评。即使没有黑沙滩和鲜艳的红色与金色服装——这些视觉元素让《苦涩的圣诞节》牢牢地归入阿尔莫多瓦的经典之作——这部电影的效果也会令人目眩。
